Returns descriptor field 4 (bytes 16-19) as a short: the bitmap handle handed to the polygon draw. Retail: mat0 record 0 = {frame 0, BlockShift 6}, record 1 = {frame 1, BlockShift 6}; at cellShift 14 that is shift 7 = 128 texels per cell, repeating every 2 cells.

entries.name: Terrain_BindTextureBank
entries.description: Binds the terrain texture bank. Takes a bare base name, joins it with the 'dba' folder pointer (PTR_DAT_004a0a28), loads that resource, and stores its 20-byte-stride frame descriptor table into _DAT_006b4fc4 for Terrain_ResolveCellTexture to index. Called from World_LoadTheater with the 4th of the five NUL-terminated strings at the end of the world<N>.wld descriptor -- so the terrain bank is named in DATA, not in code, which is exactly why neither DBSIM.EXE nor VSHELL.EXE contains the strings 'ice'/'bsnow'/'volcan'/'moon' despite those .DBA files shipping. Retail mapping: WORLD0/1 urban, 2/3 bsnow, 4/5 volcan, 6/7 ice, 8/9 moon.

entries.name: Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion
entries.description: Per-frame terrain visibility setup, called twice per frame from the frame function 0045fb9c with ActiveHeightGrid passed AS A PARAMETER (which is why a search for readers of the ActiveHeightGrid global missed the terrain render path entirely). WRITES the LOD field: grid[+0x10c] = table DAT_004a0bcc[DAT_004d1fc3] (a per-detail-setting LOD table), then >>= (cellShift - 14) when cellShift > 14 -- the engine's ported 'detailLod = cellShift > 14 ? 10 >> (cellShift-14) : 10' is this, with 10 being the retail default table entry rather than a constant. Passes grid[0x10c] << cellShift to 00428bc0 (which derives 5 distance bands), builds the visible cell-space region into grid+0x28 with count grid+0xc8 / pointer grid+0xcc / visible flag grid+0x11c, and installs two texture-basis vectors at grid+4 and grid+0x10.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellQuad
entries.description: Draws one terrain cell. Takes cellX, cellY, the HeightGrid and an output vertex block; fetches the quad's four corner cells at grid[0xec] + index*0x10 (16-byte cells), projects each corner's raw height byte (cell[0]) via 00495240 against the grid+0xd0 projection state, then resolves the cell's texture with Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(&mat0[cell[0xf] >> 2], cellX, cellY, uvOut) -- cell[0xf] >> 2 being the material index exactly as documented. Emits the quad as two triangles through 0046865c / 00468078, passing the resolved bitmap handle. Also reads cell bytes +1 and +7 via 0046bd98, which matters because the engine's HeightGrid currently treats all 14 bytes between +0x0 and +0xf as dead.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad
entries.description: Builds the terrain draw region as a square of radius (grid[+0x10c] << cellShift) world units centred on the viewer (DAT_006b4fc8 / DAT_006b4fcc), clamped to the grid's own extent ((1 << widthShift) - 2 << cellShift, plus origin at grid+0xf4/+0xf8), and emits it as a 4-corner quad at constant Z (grid+0xfc); writes count 0 instead when the clamped region is empty. Confirms the LOD field is literally a terrain draw radius in cells.

entries.name: maybe_Sim_RenderFrame
entries.description: The per-frame render function. Calls Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion(ActiveHeightGrid, view, 0), then maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects, then conditionally a second terrain setup plus maybe_Terrain_ComputeViewDistance and 0042883c, then Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate and several vtable-dispatched draws. Named 'maybe_' because the individual draw dispatches were not decoded; its role as the frame root is solid (it is the sole caller of both the terrain setup and the view setup).

entries.name: maybe_Terrain_SetDistanceBands
entries.description: Given the terrain view distance in world units (grid[+0x10c] << cellShift), computes five scaled values via 0047dfa4 against a 5-entry short table at DAT_0049abb0, storing them at DAT_004cfa0c. Shape of fog/haze band or LOD threshold setup derived from the terrain draw distance. Named 'maybe_' because the consumer of DAT_004cfa0c was not traced.

entries.name: g_UnusedTerrainTypeNames
entries.description: A 3-entry pointer table to the literal strings 'urban', 'waste', 'ruins' (at 0049ab82/0049ab88/0049ab8e); the 4th slot is not a pointer, so the table is exactly 3 long. Found via string xref while hunting terrain texture selection. DEAD DATA -- ES2FindAddressRefs on this address returns zero references anywhere in DBSIM, the third confirmed instance of this binary's dead-table pattern after g_MechTextureGroupNames and the RTTI type-name strings. Recorded so a future session does not re-derive it as a live terrain-type selector; note also that only URBAN.DBA exists in retail data (no WASTE/RUINS).

entries.name: Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres
entries.description: THE GAME'S UNIT SCALE, stated by the original itself: 'return (worldUnits / 1000) * 6', i.e. 1000 world units = 6 metres, one world unit = 6 mm, 166.667 units per metre. Three call sites, two unrelated HUD gadgets, both feeding it a raw difference of two world positions: Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator (0043c3e4, the 'WAYPOINT n: d M.' string) and the scanner MFD contact-range readout (0043ebe0/0043eecc). The integer divide quantises the displayed figure to multiples of 6 m.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator
entries.description: Per-frame HUD waypoint indicator: picks the active waypoint (or the nav-target position), computes the 2D ground distance from the player mech via Math_FastMagnitude2D, converts it with Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres, and builds the on-screen string as <prefix> + itoa(waypointNumber) + ': ' + itoa(metres) + ' M.'. Also draws the direction diamond/arrow triangles.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateSpeedReadout
entries.description: Formats the HUD speed text: itoa(Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph(LocalPlayerMech)) followed by the literal ' K/H' (0049c112). The gadget it writes into is DAT_004d185c, built in Gau_RovingGunsightWidget against the width template '000 K/H'.

entries.name: Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph
entries.description: Converts a mech's current speed to the KPH figure the HUD prints: currentSpeed * typeRec[+0xc2] / typeRec[+6], where MechType_InitOne sets typeRec[+0xc2] = Math_Q10Multiply(315, maxForwardSpeed) -- so the whole thing reduces to speed * 315/1024 (0.3076). Verified against the manual's HERC specs: OUTLAW's 325 max reads exactly 100 KPH, SAMSON's 190 reads 58 against a quoted 60, COLOSSUS 180 -> 55, MAVERICK 285 -> 88 against 90. Flyers (typeRec[+0x50] != 0, i.e. the Razor) take a different branch through the map-range helper 0047de3c. The 315 looks designer-fitted to make the fastest HERC read a round 100, so this constant should NOT be used to derive the simulation's tick length.

entries.name: Math_Q10Multiply
entries.description: Q10 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 10. Previously seen unnamed in the shield-balance code; also builds the HUD's speed-display scale factor in MechType_InitOne.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 16. Used by MechType_InitOne to rescale a mech type's speed fields by a Q16 ratio built with Math_Q16Divide.

entries.name: Math_Q16Divide
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point divide: ((int64)a << 16) / b.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 2D magnitude approximation: max(|dx|,|dy|) + min(|dx|,|dy|)/2 -- the octagonal estimate, exact on axis and up to ~11.8% high on a diagonal. The 2D counterpart of Math_FastMagnitude3D. This is the distance both HUD distance readouts display, so the original's own on-screen ranges carry that error.

entries.name: maybe_Math_MapRange
entries.description: Five-argument linear remap: maps param_1 from the range [param_2,param_3] onto [param_4,param_5] with a rounding bias term. Named 'maybe_' because it was only observed in one place (the flyer branch of Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph).

entries.name: Time_GetCoarseTicks
entries.description: (GetTickCount() - startTick) >> 4, i.e. elapsed time in 16 ms units (62.5 Hz). The mission clock gadget (0043dcac) advances one displayed second per 0x3c=60 of these units, so the original's clock runs ~4% fast. This is the coarse UI/event timebase and is NOT the same thing as SimTickDelta, which Sim_MainTick reads from a separate per-frame timing struct.

entries.name: Vec2_Subtract
entries.description: In-place 2D vector subtract: a->x -= b->x, a->y -= b->y. Confirms the HUD's waypoint/contact distances are ground-plane distances, Z ignored.

entries.name: Vec2_Magnitude
entries.description: Thin wrapper: Math_FastMagnitude2D(v->x, v->y) via 0049298e.

entries.name: Vec2_DistanceBetween
entries.description: Copies a 2D point, subtracts another (Vec2_Subtract) and returns the approximate magnitude (Vec2_Magnitude) -- the distance primitive the HUD waypoint indicator uses.

entries.name: DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects
entries.description: DBSIM's world-spawn pass and the function that actually builds a mission's objects -- the second of two reads of data\script.dat. RE-OPENS the file from the top (path built from maybe_DatFolderPrefixPtr + the string at 0049aa3e), skips blocks 1-6, then walks blocks 7-13 again. For every slot DBSim_LoadScriptDat's first pass marked live it constructs an object and reads that object's OWN record for placement: block 7 (134B) gives mech type at +0x28, weapon fit at +0x2a, position ref at +0x3e, heading ref at +0x40; block 8 (92B) gives position +0x28, heading +0x2a, flyer type +0x2c; block 9 (52B) gives base type +0x00, position +0x02, heading +0x04. Position refs resolve into the block-1 coordinate array (DAT_004a9e90, stride 0xc); heading refs into the pre-multiplied block-2 array (DAT_004a9e94). Mechs and bases get Terrain_HeightQuery plus the type's foot offset; flyers get no query. It then reads block 11 into DAT_004a9e84 (stride 0x7a) via DBSim_BuildGroupRecord, remapping member refs to dense object indices, and appends the player.mec lance in place of record 0's members. This function is why script-dat.md's earlier 'DBSIM discards the placement data' description was wrong -- that described pass 1 only.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildGroupRecord
entries.description: Builds one script.dat block-11 record into a 0x7a-byte in-memory group record: discriminator (record +0x28) at group+0, formation id (+0x2a) at group+2, heading value at group+10, the resolved block-1 coordinate pointer at group+0x18, the resolved row-10 action pointer at group+0x14, and an allocated array of member object pointers at group+0xc. Then attaches every populated member by discriminator -- Mech_AttachToGroup (0/mechs), FUN_00421ee8 (1/flyers), FUN_00405c3c (2/bases) -- passing each its slot index within the group.

entries.name: Mech_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a mech to its mission group: stores the group pointer at mech+0x45 and the member slot index at mech+0x49, then fills in heading and position ONLY IF still at the -0x8000 'unset' sentinel -- which is why a roster record's own position ref wins where set and the group's point is the fallback. Position comes from the group's coordinate pointer (group+0x18), or from FUN_00423b0c against the group's route when that is null. Z is Terrain_HeightQuery plus the mech type's foot offset (typeRecord+0x16), plus 5000 when typeRecord+0x50 is set. Calls mech vtable +0x78 (Mech_ApplyFormationOffset) with the position first. FUN_00421ee8 and FUN_00405c3c are the flyer and base equivalents; the flyer one deliberately does no terrain query and substitutes z=5000 when the coordinate's z is zero.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x78. Spreads a group's members around its spawn point. No-ops for slot 0 (the leader stands on the point exactly); otherwise looks up Formation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id at group+2, mech+0x49) and hands the offset to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset, which rotates it by the group leader's heading before adding it to the position.

entries.name: Formation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Returns a static 3-short {x, y, 0} formation offset: table[formationId * 0x1c + slot * 4 - 4] and the short after it. So a formation is 28 bytes = seven (x, y) short pairs, covering follower slots 1-7. OPEN: the table pointer _DAT_004a9df0 has exactly one reference in the whole binary -- this read -- and lives in uninitialised data, so nothing links it to a file. dat\MFORMS.DAT fits the shape exactly (142 content bytes = count + five 28-byte formations, formation 0 a symmetric wedge at 10000-unit steps) but is unconfirmed. Contrast the base equivalent (FUN_00405b9c/Base_LoadFormationTable, 2026-08-14), whose load site IS confirmed -- this pointer never got the same treatment.

entries.name: Formation_RotateAndAddOffset
entries.description: Rotates a formation offset into world space and adds it to a position. Takes the group leader (first entry of the group's member array at group+0xc), lazily builds its rotation matrix from its heading (leader+0xc -> leader+0x12, guarded by the stale flag at leader+0x32 that Mech_AttachToGroup clears), rotates the offset by it, and accumulates into the caller's x/y/z. Also the base-formation attach path's rotator (called from FUN_00405c04); for a heading-only object (no pitch/roll, true of every base) the matrix build (FUN_0047eaac) plus apply (FUN_0047fedc) reduces algebraically to a plain 2D rotation: worldDX = dx*cos(heading) - dy*sin(heading), worldDY = dx*sin(heading) + dy*cos(heading).

entries.name: Base_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Base/structure equivalent of Mech_AttachToGroup (00417aa8), called from DBSim_BuildGroupRecord (00423b34) for discriminator 2. Stores the group pointer at +0x45 and the member's slot index within the group's DiscriminatedRefs array at +0x49. Fills heading only if unset (-0x8000 sentinel), applying a per-slot heading nudge from a formation-indexed table when the slot is nonzero. Fills position only if unset: reads the group's own coordinate pointer (group+0x18) or falls back to its route (FUN_00423b0c), then -- only when the caller's BinaryFlag arg (the raw block-11 record's own 0x06 field) is nonzero -- snaps that shared point to a per-formation grid (fields the C# port does not model; see BaseFormationTable's doc comment) before unconditionally calling the object's own vtable +0x78 (Base_ApplyFormationOffset, FUN_00405c04) with the position, then a terrain height query.

entries.name: Base_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Vtable +0x78 for every base subtype (confirmed identical across all five base vtables: 0x497940/0x4979d4/0x4978ac/0x497784/0x497818, each layered on the common base vtable 0x49a54c) -- the structural match for Mech_ApplyFormationOffset (00417898). No-ops when the object's group-relative slot (+0x49) is 0 (the group's first-claimed member); otherwise looks up BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id, slot) via FUN_00405b9c and hands the offset to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset (00411d64).

entries.name: BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Base equivalent of Formation_GetSlotOffset (004205cc), but reading a variable-length, file-backed table instead of a flat one: DAT_004a9630[formationId] is a per-formation record whose +4 field is a pointer to that formation's slot-offset array (10 bytes/slot: two int32s X,Y then a trailing int16), indexed as ptr + (slot-1)*10 -- i.e. slot N uses the (N-1)-th entry, so slot 1 (the group's first follower) uses entry 0. Returns {x, y} as two int32s (z is a one-time-zeroed static, never written per-call -- bases take no Z offset). DAT_004a9630 is populated by Base_LoadResources (00405fac) from dat\BFORMS.DAT -- unlike the mech table, this load site IS confirmed.

entries.name: Base_LoadResources
entries.description: base.cpp's resource-load sequence for the base/structure subsystem: streams dat\bforms (-> DAT_004a9630, formation offsets; see BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset), dat\lc_wpns, dat\bases (-> DAT_004a9620, the BASES.DAT type table BaseTypeTable.cs also reads; this is the only reader of it -- an entry at 0043a2e0 carried a copy of this description under the name Bases_LoadTypeTable until 2026-08-18, when that address was identified as MfdStatusScreen_Ctor and renamed), dat\basecol (collision), dat\bhulks, dat\basetex and dat\vehtex (texture banks) via a shared plain-file-read helper (FUN_00472e08 open / FUN_004734ac read via a vtable+0x18 dispatch / FUN_00472e58 close -- no container header, first bytes of each file are its own content, confirmed against BASES.DAT's independently-verified byte-exact parse). BFORMS.DAT's per-formation record is fully variable-length: int32 slot count N, N*10 bytes of slot data, an int32 + two more int32s (grid-snap fields, unmodelled), an int32 buffer count M, then M {1 length byte + that many data bytes} buffers -- confirmed byte-exact: walking the retail file this way consumes all 3186 content bytes with 17 formations (matching the block-11 formation id field's documented 0-16 range) and nothing left over.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's status screen, shared by mode 0 (STATUS, F1) and mode 4 (TARGET, F5) -- MfdDisplay_Ctor builds one of each. Lazily loads the `bases`, `vehicles` and `flyers` sprite banks (folder "hba"/"dba" off VideoMode_UseHiResBanks) for target silhouettes, sets the wireframe viewport to inset+(0x2d,0xd)-(0x5f,0x3a), and builds five text labels from tables at 0049bd84 (x0), 0049bd8e (y0) and 0049bd98 (font selector into {ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE, [14] RED}). CORRECTED 2026-08-18: was named Bases_LoadTypeTable. It does not read dat\BASES.DAT -- that is Base_LoadResources (0043a3xx family, see its own entry); the collision was between loading the BASES sprite bank and loading the BASES data file. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: BaseType_LoadShape
entries.description: The whole of a structure type's model selection, indexing dat\BASES.DAT's table at typeIndex * 0x3c: the field at +6 picks the library (0 -> dgs\bases via BaseType_ResolveShape with classId 0x2bc0001, else dts\bases_an via the animated-library path with 0x1e0003) and the field at +2 is the shape index within it; the field at +0x32 picks the texture bank (0 -> basetex, else vehtex, except type 0x34 which borrows RAZOR's mech bank). Cross-check: exactly eight types select the animated library and BASES_AN.DTS holds exactly eight roots, numbered as those eight reference them. CORRECTED 2026-08-14: the 0x2bc0001/0x1e0003 constants are not recordSize<<16|version -- they are ClassItem registry classIds, and 0x2bc0001 is literally BASES.DGS's own leading 4 bytes. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: BaseType_ResolveShape
entries.description: Resolves one dgs\bases shape by index (called by BaseType_LoadShape): reopens the file, then loops calling the ClassItem peek/skip primitive (FUN_0047a1fc, then FUN_0047a2a8 to skip) until the requested index is reached, then calls ClassItem_LoadResource once for the real load. Confirms dgs\BASES.DGS/BHULKS.DGS are flat sequential ClassItem lists, not random-access. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: BaseShape_Construct
entries.description: ClassItem registry loadFn for classId 0x02bc0001 (dgs\bases/bhulks shape records): allocates a 0x438-byte object, installs the class's vtable (0049aaa0), then calls vtable+0xc (BaseShape_ReadFromStream). See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: BaseShape_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Field reader for a dgs\bases/bhulks shape record (vtable+0xc for classId 0x02bc0001), on top of the generic ClassItem base-class chain (FUN_00490d5c). Reads 5 int16 scalars, a fixed 1024-byte block, then (if the 2nd scalar/sub-record count is nonzero) that many raw sub-records sized by the 1st scalar. Byte-verified against the retail file -- see dgs-hd0-notes.md and HercWorks.Core.Io.Transform.Dbsim.BasesDgsTransformer for the full record shape including the levels below.

entries.name: ClassItemTree_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Generic base-class reader shared by dgs\bases/bhulks shape records (one level up from BaseShape_ReadFromStream): reads two int16 counts, a parallel int16 array, and a per-entry 32-byte vector (undecoded -- consumed by a BSP-adjacent walk, FUN_00476a1c). Byte-verified as part of the full record shape -- see dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: ClassItemTree_ReadChildren
entries.description: Generic base-class reader (below ClassItemTree_ReadFromStream): reads an int16 child count then that many nested objects via ClassItem_LoadResource. For dgs\bases/bhulks shape records, every retail child is an ordinary TSObjectHeader-family DTS chunk (observed tag 0x0014000c = TSDetailPart) -- the key finding that lets DTSModelTransformer.ReadOneObject parse it directly. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: ClassItemTree_ReadBaseHeader
entries.description: Deepest base-class reader in the ClassItem shape-tree hierarchy: 3 int16 id/name fields + 6 raw bytes. Shared by dgs\bases/bhulks shape records. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: LoadNameList
entries.description: Loads a nam\<name>.NAM list -- a flat run of NUL-terminated ASCII names indexed by type number -- with a capacity bound as the second argument. Called with ('mechs', 0x55) into the mech name table DAT_004a9de4 that MechType_InitOne indexes, and with ('flyers', 0x22) into DAT_004a9e74. These are the tables that turn script.dat block 7's and block 8's type numbers into resource base names; MECHS.NAM ships 21 names and FLYERS.NAM 3.

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Construct
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real constructor, found via g_TSObjectTypeRegistry's tag=0x00140002 entry. Same Watcom multi-base-class stamping pattern as TSTexture4Poly_Construct, finishing with &PTR_FUN_0047ee38 -- the actually-used TSSolidPoly vtable at runtime. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_TSSolidPolyVtable
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real, fully-constructed vtable (found via TSSolidPoly_Construct's final vtable-pointer stamp). Slot +0x1c (TSSolidPoly_Render, FUN_00422a32) is what TSGroup_RenderPolys's per-poly dispatch (*(*polyPtr)+0x1c) calls for a TSSolidPoly, mirroring TSTexture4Poly's g_TSTexture4PolyVtable +0x1c slot exactly.

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real vtable-slot-0x1c render method (see g_TSSolidPolyVtable). Resolves surface record via (ColorIndexId*4 + g_ActiveSurfaceRecords) -- same *4 stride as TSTexture4Poly_Render, independently reconfirming ColorIndexId=surfaceIndex*4. Runs maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest against poly+4/+6 (Normal/Center point indices, each *6 into the Vec3Short point array) to pick front (piVar3[0]/[1] = Front/FrontLine) or back (piVar3[2]/[3] = Back/BackLine) color pair -- confirms TSSurfaceEntry's 4-slot Front/FrontLine/Back/BackLine layout applies to flat polys too, not just textured ones. Skips drawing if both resolved color dwords have top byte 0x18-shift == 0x14 (looks like an uninitialized/sentinel guard, not chased further). Otherwise clips via FUN_0045e694/FUN_0045ec54 and fills via FUN_0045f364 -- the SAME flat/solid 2D fill chain TSTexture4Poly_Render's DAT_00471890!=0 fallback branch also uses, confirming that branch really is 'reuse the flat-poly fill path' as its name implies. No dithering/lighting-ramp math visible anywhere in this chain -- VSHELL (a shell/viewer app) passes FrontColor/BackColor straight through to the fill routines, unlike DBSIM's in-mission renderer.

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: CONFIRMED (upgraded from the prior handoff's 'inferred, not proven') to be DBSIM's flat/solid-poly render function, by structural match against VSHELL's independently RTTI-registry-verified TSSolidPoly_Render (FUN_00422a32): both resolve their surface record via (ColorIndexId*4 + surfaceRecordsBase) (here _DAT_006c697a), both call a front/back visibility test (FUN_0048c620 here, the DBSIM counterpart of maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest) against poly+4/+6 Normal/Center point indices (*6 stride), both pick a Front or Back color-pair from the resulting surface record. DBSIM's version additionally computes a per-face lighting 'shade' byte via FUN_0048bedc (still undecoded) and, when DAT_004a5b1c (the loaded world<N>.rmp ramp) is set, uses it to build a ramp-table byte offset (local_24 = (DAT_004a5b1c-1)*shade & 0xffffff00 + _DAT_004a5b18) before dispatching to FUN_00468078/FUN_0046865c -> ... -> FUN_0046ac48's dither+ramp pixel formula. This is the function documented in docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md; that doc's open question #1 (confirm this is really the flat/solid poly renderer) is now closed.

entries.name: TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest
entries.description: DBSIM's counterpart to VSHELL's maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest -- called identically (two Vec3Short point pointers, Normal then Center) from TSSolidPoly_Render (FUN_00474e9c) to pick front vs. back surface color. Confirmed via structural match, not independently disassembled instruction-by-instruction.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeForFace
entries.description: The per-face 'shade byte' (0-255, clamped) calculation feeding TSSolidPoly_Render's lighting-ramp lookup. NOT a simple angle calc -- a real light-accumulation loop over the active light list (DAT_006c6130, max 10 slots, count DAT_006c612c), dispatching per-entry on a type tag from FUN_0048d94b: type 0 = ambient (adds a flat intensity from FUN_0048d956 unconditionally -- never seen actually populated this session, see Light_AddDirectional/PointHelper's entries), type 1 = directional (dot-product-like test via FUN_0048d99b against the face's Normal point (param_1), only contributes when the result crosses a fixed threshold, i.e. face-vs-light-direction test), type 2 = point light (distance-attenuated: displacement from the light's position (FUN_0048d961) to the face's Center point (param_2) combined with the Normal via FUN_0048d86e, divided by distance/range fields FUN_0048d973/FUN_0048d97e). Params: param_1 = poly's Normal-index Vec3Short pointer, param_2 = poly's Center-index Vec3Short pointer (same two pointers TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest receives). Sibling functions FUN_0048bdcc/FUN_0048c060 are near-identical variants (different param shapes) used elsewhere for the same shade calc, likely per-vertex vs. per-face evaluation.

entries.name: Light_Register
entries.description: Adds a light object pointer to the active light list (DAT_006c6130, 10-slot max, dedups by pointer identity). Only 4 call sites in the whole binary: FUN_00407388/FUN_00407444 (pooled directional/point light getters, see their own entries), FUN_00407878 (re-registers a persistent light list DAT_004a9690 into the active manager), and Sim_InitMissionSession (FUN_004614fc, inlines the same directional-light-creation logic as FUN_00407388 and calls this directly).

entries.name: Light_GetOrCreateDirectional
entries.description: Pooled-object getter/constructor for a type=1 (directional) light: recycles from a small free-list at param_1+0x35c/+0x360 if available, otherwise allocates+constructs (vtable &PTR_LAB_0049f8d8, type field at +0x16 set to 1), then registers it via Light_Register (FUN_0048bd44). Not yet traced who calls this (likely weapon/effect spawn code, not chased this session -- out of scope for static mission-geometry lighting).

entries.name: Light_GetOrCreatePoint
entries.description: Same pooled-object pattern as Light_GetOrCreateDirectional (FUN_00407388) but for a type=2 (point) light (vtable &PTR_LAB_00497ac8, type field +0x16 set to 2). Likely explosion/muzzle-flash light spawning; callers not traced this session.

entries.name: Light_CreateMissionSun
entries.description: MAJOR FINDING: called exactly once per mission, unconditionally, from Sim_InitMissionSession (FUN_004614fc) right after the light-system reset (FUN_0048dbfc) and before DBSim_LoadScriptDat -- creates the ONE directional 'sun' light every mission gets. Direction is NOT read from any mission/theater file: it's built from two HARDCODED constant vectors, local_38=(0,0x1000,0) and local_40=(-6000,0,21000), combined via FUN_0047eaac (looks like a normalize/transform) then FUN_0047ffb4 (looks like it derives a direction from a target-point + up-vector pair, output stored as the light's direction field). Intensity is set via vtable+4 call with literal 0x100 (256). The created light is registered via Light_Register (FUN_0048bd44) AND pushed onto a persistent list (DAT_004a9690) via FUN_00407800, so it survives a later Light_ReregisterPersistent (FUN_00407878) call. No separate ambient (type=0) light creation was found anywhere in the binary this session -- Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-0 branch may be genuinely unused by real missions, meaning faces angled away from the sun likely render fully unlit (shade=0), not floor-lit. FUN_0047eaac/FUN_0047ffb4/FUN_0048d99b (the actual per-face dot-product math) are NOT yet decoded -- needed for a byte-exact reimplementation, but the qualitative shape (single fixed sun direction+intensity, no mission-specific lighting data) is now solid enough to plan an engine implementation around.

entries.name: Sim_InitMissionSession
entries.description: Per-mission session setup: resets the light system (FUN_0048dbfc), creates the mission's one hardcoded sun light (Light_CreateMissionSun), then calls DBSim_LoadScriptDat and DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects. Confirms lighting setup happens once per mission load, independent of which script.dat/theater is loaded.

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14
entries.description: Builds a 3x3 rotation matrix (9 Q14 fixed-point shorts + 1 mode byte, 10 shorts total output) from a Vec3Short of Euler angles (param_1), using a sin/cos lookup table at DAT_004a25dc (1024-entry quarter-wave table, angle unit = 0x10000 per full circle, i.e. raw/65536*360 = degrees). Has a fast-path when the X and Y angle components are both zero (2-axis-only case, cos/sin of Z alone); otherwise builds the general 3-axis matrix via the standard trig-table-driven approach (same trig-table technique as the sim's other rotation math, see [[project_es2_terrain_format]]-adjacent RE). Called by Light_CreateMissionSun with angles (-6000, 0, 21000) -- confirms the sun's direction is computed, not stored as a literal vector.

entries.name: RotateVectorByMatrixQ14
entries.description: Matrix-vector multiply: rotates param_1 (Vec3Short) by the 3x3 Q14 matrix param_2 (as built by BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14), writing the result to param_3. Has fast-paths for the matrix's degenerate mode byte (param_2[9]) similar to the matrix builder's own fast path. Called by Light_CreateMissionSun as rotate((0,0x1000,0), sunRotationMatrix) -- i.e. the sun's direction is 'straight up' rotated by the fixed Euler angles, not an arbitrary hand-authored vector.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Short
entries.description: Literal 3-component dot product on two Vec3Short pointers: a.x*b.x+a.y*b.y+a.z*b.z, no scaling/clamping. Called (via the Light_ComputeShadeForFace accessor wrapper FUN_0048d99b) with the poly's Normal-index point and a directional light's own direction vector -- confirms the type-1 (directional) lighting term in Light_ComputeShadeForFace is a plain dot product, i.e. the poly's 'Normal' auxiliary point genuinely holds a normal-like vector (not a position), consistent with the earlier front/back visibility-test finding that Normal/Center are auxiliary vertex-index fields used for facing math, not literal mesh geometry.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Int
entries.description: Same as DotProductVec3Short but on int (not short) components -- used by Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-2 (point light) branch after converting the light-to-face displacement into ints.

entries.name: World_LoadTheater
entries.description: SUPERSEDES the prior entry's 'ramp/LUT's own consumer is still untraced' note -- now fully closed. world<N>.rmp's real format, BYTE-VERIFIED against all 10 retail files (WORLD0-9.RMP, all exactly 98312 bytes): int32 width, int32 height, then width*height*256 raw bytes (all 10 files: width=32, height=12, 8+32*12*256=98312, exact match). The loader reads width/height via the same generic field-reader callback used for .wld fields, then reads the whole width*height*256 body in one call into DAT_004a09b0 (FUN_004734ac(fileHandle, width*height*256, DAT_004a09b0)). Installs _DAT_004a5b18=rampTableBase, DAT_004a5b1c=width, DAT_004a5b20=width (both set to width, not height -- 'height' i.e. 12 is read and used locally for the allocation size but not retained in any global this session found). Cross-referencing TSSolidPoly_Render's ramp-offset formula ((DAT_004a5b1c-1)*shade & 0xffffff00 -- i.e. (width-1)*shade rounded down to a multiple of 256) confirms 'width'=32 is the light-level-row COUNT and each row is 256 bytes (one byte per dither-table output 0-255), i.e. TSSolidPoly_Render only ever reads from the FIRST 32*256=8192-byte block of the file's 98304-byte body -- the other 11 height-slices are not consumed by this code path (unknown purpose, not chased -- possibly a different render mode's ramp bank, e.g. gouraud/texture-modulate).
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 follow-up (real-file probe against E:\ES2Stuff\ES2\VOL\rmp\WORLD*.RMP via GameContent), docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md

entries.name: maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache
entries.description: CORRECTS this entry's own prior 'static compiled-in dither table' claim from earlier the same session -- that was WRONG. DBSIM.EXE's total file size is 724,512 bytes; this address sits in the DATA section's second (huge, 2,245,120-byte) chunk, which is almost certainly BSS-style zero-fill reserved space, not literal file content, ruling out a ~16MB static table outright. Traced the real populator: FUN_00469d10 (a rectangle-packing cache-insertion routine, recurses into an overflow bank via param_1[0x200]/[0x201] when a 256-wide row is full) and its wrapper FUN_00469f38 (allocates a 20-byte-stride descriptor per inserted image via Cpp_VectorNew, matching the SAME stride as TSTexture4Poly's already-solved g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] frame-descriptor table). FUN_00469f38 is called from 7 places across totally unrelated subsystems -- Base_LoadResources, maybe_Ground_LoadFlatShapes, Weapons_LoadResourceTables, Terrain_BindTextureBank, and two weapon-effect loaders (bullets.cpp/beam.cpp equivalents, FUN_0040ade0/FUN_0040b6e0) -- each packing a freshly-loaded DBA's frames into this SAME shared atlas via FUN_0045cdd8 (DBA loader). CONCLUSION: this is a generic runtime bitmap/texture atlas cache shared by the whole engine (mechs, weapons, terrain, ground shapes), not a purpose-built dither table. TSSolidPoly_Render's (colorField<<16 | pixelCoord) addressing therefore means 'sample pixel pixelCoord from cached bitmap slot colorField', not 'look up a fixed dither pattern' -- meaning the earlier assumption that colorField=FrontColor (a 0-255 palette index) is now suspect; it more plausibly indexes a specific SMALL-N cached bitmap slot (a dither/shading swatch loaded once per theater), which would also explain why the naive 16MB address range is never actually exercised. WHICH atlas slot TSSolidPoly_Render's shading swatch specifically occupies, and who inserts it, was NOT found this session -- none of the 7 known FUN_00469f38 callers is an obvious 'load lighting dither pattern' site. This is now the real open question, distinct from and more specific than 'extract the dither table's raw bytes'.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 follow-up (correction pass), docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md

entries.name: g_CurrentShapeDbaContext
entries.description: RESOLVES handoff item #6/#8. Set once per shape instance by FUN_0042fa18 (maybe_TSShapeInstance_PrepareRenderContext) as `param_1 + 0x1a`, i.e. a pointer into the per-shape render object -- the exact same offset pattern as VSHELL's TSShapeInstance+0x26 bound-DBA field, just a different struct layout. g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] (== param_1+0x1e) is the shape's currently-bound DBA's 20-byte-stride frame-descriptor table -- THE SAME g_ActiveBitmapArray[1]-equivalent table TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes for UV corners. TSSolidPoly_Render (FUN_00474e9c) uses `g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] + FrontColor*0x14` to fetch a frame descriptor, then reads its field+0x10 (the 5th int32, F4 -- previously found to be a 'texture-data pointer/handle' in the TSTexture4Poly descriptor) as the value shifted into the shared bitmap atlas (maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache/DAT_004d4f88) bank selector for ordered-dither pixel fill.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation)

entries.name: maybe_TSShapeInstance_PrepareRenderContext
entries.description: Per-shape-instance render setup, called once before a shape's polys are drawn. Installs g_CurrentShapeDbaContext (DAT_006c60e8 = param_1+0x1a) and the surface-record base (_DAT_006c697a = param_1+0x61) that TSSolidPoly_Render/TSTexture4Poly-equivalent poly renderers read from -- i.e. this is where 'the currently bound DBA' becomes visible to the poly-render layer for this shape, DBSIM's counterpart to VSHELL's TSShapeInstance_Render save/swap/restore step. Also does per-point LOD/pop rotation math (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 per point) unrelated to texturing. Name is a guess from structural role, not from an RTTI/registry match.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation)

entries.name: maybe_TSGouraudOrSimilarPoly_Render
entries.description: Sibling poly-render function reusing g_CurrentShapeDbaContext/_DAT_006c697a exactly like TSSolidPoly_Render (same ColorIndexId*4 surface lookup, same FrontColor-indexes-frame-descriptor-table pattern feeding FUN_00468078 as the 4th arg). Not yet matched to a specific TSPoly subtype via the RTTI registry -- flagged here only because it shares and thus corroborates the g_CurrentShapeDbaContext mechanism.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation)

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: SUPERSEDES this entry's earlier 'material-record populator untraced' note -- CLOSES handoff #6 and #8. There is no dedicated 'lighting swatch' DBA anywhere in the binary -- that was the wrong mental model. TSSolidPoly_Render resolves its surface record (ColorIndexId*4 + surfaceRecordsBase, as before), then uses that record's FrontColor/BackColor value as a FRAME INDEX into g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] -- the SAME per-shape bound-DBA frame-descriptor table TSTexture4Poly_Render reads for UV corners (see g_CurrentShapeDbaContext). It reads that frame descriptor's field+0x10 (F4, the bitmap-data handle) and feeds it into the shared bitmap-atlas dither/ramp pixel-fill chain (FUN_00468078/FUN_0046865c -> ... -> FUN_0046ac48) as the atlas bank selector. PRACTICAL UPSHOT: a flat-shaded face's FrontColor selects a FRAME of whichever texture bank is already bound to that mesh (BASETEX.DBA for buildings, a mech's own weight-class bank for mechs, etc. -- see docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md) -- not a raw palette index and not a separate asset. Herculan.Engine already decodes and GPU-uploads every one of these banks for textured rendering, so a byte-faithful reimplementation needs no new bitmap loader for this step, only: (1) a world<N>.rmp reader (format solved, see World_LoadTheater), (2) sampling the mesh's own already-loaded bank at frame=FrontColor as the dither swatch, (3) the sun-light dot-product shade calc (Light_ComputeShadeForFace).
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation), docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md

entries.name: g_TSPolyUseAltPath_maybeDead
entries.description: CLOSES handoff #7. Read-only byte: 6 read sites (TSSolidPoly_Render x5, maybe_TSGouraudOrSimilarPoly_Render x1), ZERO write sites found anywhere in DBSIM.EXE (checked via getReferencesTo across the whole binary). Read directly from the mapped image (ES2ReadDataValue.java): value is 0, in an initialized/file-backed (not BSS) DATA block -- i.e. this is a compile-time constant baked into the shipped exe, not a runtime-toggled setting, same pattern as VSHELL's DAT_00471890 (g_UseFlatPolyFallback) in the sibling ThreeSpace codebase. Since every reader branches on `==0`/`!=0` and the byte is permanently 0, the `==0` branch (the one solved in handoff #6: local_c/g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] frame lookup, FUN_00468078 dispatch) is the ONLY branch that ever executes in retail DBSIM.EXE. The `!=0` branch (local_28-based lookup, FUN_0048c848/FUN_0048cfec/FUN_0048d518) is dead code in the shipped game and does not need reverse engineering for a faithful Herculan.Engine implementation.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 third follow-up (#7 closure)

entries.name: g_TSSolidPolyRasterizerVariant_maybeDead
entries.description: Same dead-constant pattern as g_TSPolyUseAltPath_maybeDead (0049f26c): single read site (TSSolidPoly_Render, selects FUN_00468078 vs FUN_0046865c), zero write sites anywhere in DBSIM.EXE, value read directly from the image is 0 in an initialized DATA block. FUN_00468078 is therefore confirmed as the only rasterizer dispatch target ever taken in retail for TSSolidPoly.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 third follow-up (#7 closure)

entries.name: Mech_LoadResources
entries.description: mechsys.cpp's resource-load sequence for the mech subsystem -- the mech-side twin of Base_LoadResources (00405fac). Resets the mech-type-slot table (memset &DAT_004a9d8c, 0xff, 0x55), then streams dat\mforms (string 'mforms' at 0049a46b, joined with the shared 'dat' folder-prefix helper FUN_00492ae0): reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9dec, allocates that many 28-byte vector elements (Cpp_VectorNew(..., 0x1c, count, ...) -- 7 (x,y) int16 pairs/formation, matching Formation_GetSlotOffset's stride), stores the vector pointer into _DAT_004a9df0 (previously unwritten anywhere in disassembled code -- see that symbol's updated entry), then reads count*28 bytes straight from the file into the buffer. Afterwards loads the 7 mech texture groups (g_MechTextureGroupNames/g_MechTextureGroupSlots) via FUN_0045cdd8/FUN_00469f38, unrelated to formations. This function was never auto-disassembled by prior analysis passes (it sits directly after another function's RET with no call-graph edge Ghidra had found, so nothing walked into it) -- found by raw byte-scanning for the 'mforms' string's address as a PUSH-immediate operand, then manually disassembling/decompiling from there. Registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via a thunk at 00420654 (FUN_00401d64(Mech_LoadResources, 2)), confirming it is live code the game runs, not dead weight.
entries.source: docs/formats/script-dat.md 2026-08-14 (mech formation spread, resolving the MFORMS.DAT load-site gap)

entries.name: g_MechFormationTable
entries.description: The mech formation-offset table pointer Formation_GetSlotOffset (004205cc) reads. Previously documented as having no write site anywhere in DBSIM.EXE -- that was true only of the code Ghidra had disassembled; Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0), found 2026-08-14, writes it (`_DAT_004a9df0 = extraout_EAX_00;` immediately after Cpp_VectorNew allocates count*28 bytes and before the file's formation data is read into that buffer). Sits in a tight cluster of mech-subsystem globals: DAT_004a9de4 (mech name table, LoadNameList's target) / DAT_004a9dec (formation count) / this pointer / DAT_004a9df4 (cached object-pool handle, maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: Mech_RegisterLoader
entries.description: Thunk that registers Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0) into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via FUN_00401d64(Mech_LoadResources, 2), then separately allocates the 7-slot mech-texture-group vector (Cpp_VectorNew(&g_MechTextureGroupSlots, 8, 8, 1, ...)). Found by raw dword-scanning DBSIM.EXE for Mech_LoadResources' address used as a PUSH-immediate operand (68 B0 FD 41 00); like Mech_LoadResources itself, was never auto-disassembled by prior analysis (sits right after another function's RET, no call-graph edge into it).

entries.name: RegisterSubsystemLoader
entries.description: Appends (funcPtr, id) to a global registration table (DAT_004a80d0, 6-byte entries: 4-byte function pointer + 2-byte id) at the slot indexed by a global counter (DAT_00497074) that it then increments. Confirms whatever registers itself here -- e.g. Mech_LoadResources via the 00420654 thunk -- is walked and invoked by DBSIM's generic subsystem-init driver rather than being dead code.

entries.name: s_mforms_0049a46b
entries.description: String literal 'mforms', mechsys.cpp's dat\MFORMS.DAT resource name (joined with the 'dat' folder prefix by FUN_00492ae0 in Mech_LoadResources). Sits in a literal pool alongside other mechsys.cpp string constants (difficulty names, texture-bank names) immediately followed by the source-file name 'mechsys.cpp' itself -- typical MSVC layout for a translation unit's string constants. No Reference object existed to this address before Mech_LoadResources was manually disassembled, because that function itself was never auto-analyzed; found by raw byte-scanning every initialized memory block for the literal ASCII bytes.

entries.name: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName
entries.description: The shared folder\name resource-path builder: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(name, folder) writes 'folder\\name' into a shared static buffer (&DAT_006cbcae) via FUN_00492a84(name) + strcat('\\') + strcat(folder). Confirmed by tracing its two operands against known-good results (e.g. ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, "vue") and the folder-name pointer table at CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames). Matches Herculan.Engine.Content.GameContent's own folder\name resolution convention exactly -- this is DBSIM's side of the same addressing scheme.

entries.name: CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames
entries.description: A 12-entry constant pointer table of resource folder-name strings: dpl, gl, dmg, col, edg, dba, dci, dfn, gau, hfn, hdg, hba (0x4a0a14-0x4a0a43, pointing into a shared string pool at 0x4a0a44 that separately also holds wb/rb (fopen modes) and nam/dat/bnd/dts, those last four belonging to a different, not-yet-located table). Despite the name, this table is NOT cockpit-exclusive -- gau/dpl/dba/dci/dfn/hfn/hdg/hba are all mech-subsystem resource kinds reused site-wide; named for the first confirmed use found this session (index 0, "dpl", is PTR_DAT_004a0a14, used directly by the COCKPIT.DPL/IMPACTCP.DPL load calls -- see CockpitPaletteSingleton).

entries.name: CockpitPaletteSingleton
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-loaded cockpit-family DynamixPalette object. First loaded lazily (guarded by == 0) as the literal resource 'dpl\\cockpit' (s_cockpit_0049ae69 + CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames[0]="dpl", via ResourcePath_BuildFolderName + ClassItem_LoadTaggedResource) -- confirms DBSIM loads COCKPIT.DPL by a plain literal name, not a derived/offset one, and the real retail file ES2/VOL/simvol0/dpl/COCKPIT.DPL exists under exactly that name. Later swapped to 'dpl\\impactcp' (IMPACTCP.DPL, also a real retail file) as a second, smaller damage/impact-flash palette, whose colors get copied into a 24-entry sub-range of the global active display palette (Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, ...)) rather than replacing CockpitPaletteSingleton wholesale. No index-remap/offset was found anywhere in this load path -- decoding a real .HB0 through COCKPIT.DPL with a direct, unmodified index lookup produces a correct, recognizable cockpit image (visually verified against APOCA.HB0/SAMSON.HB0), settling Milestone 8 Phase 0 Q1: the existing TextureViewerForm.PreferredPaletteFor("COCKPIT") heuristic is exactly right, not merely a plausible guess.

entries.name: Palette_InstallRange
entries.description: Palette_InstallRange(baseIndex, count, srcRgbaArray): copies count RGBA/RGB entries from srcRgbaArray into the global active display palette (*(DAT_0049b020+8) + baseIndex*4), then tracks the min/max dirty index range (DAT_0049b028/DAT_0049b02c) for a batched hardware palette update -- classic indexed-display-mode palette management. Used by the cockpit-view constructor to install the small IMPACTCP.DPL flash palette into a 24-entry sub-range (base 0x2a) of the shared 256-slot palette, distinct from CockpitPaletteSingleton's own local RGB array.

entries.name: CockpitViewInstance
entries.description: Singleton pointer to LocalPlayerMech's live cockpit/HUD view object (set once, guarded by == 0, in ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll/00431098). Directly embeds each GAU widget as a live sub-object at a fixed struct offset matching GAUFile.cs's own documented field order: a 10-slot weapon-button array at +0x1c (matches GAU's 10 weapon hardpoint slots), then single widgets at +0x1e1/+0x1e5/+0x1e9/+0x1ed/+0x1f1/+0x1f5/+0x1f9/+0x20b (chain/link/autotrack/energy-meter-family offsets), each paint-dispatched via its own vtable call. Read throughout the cockpit/HUD call graph (Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, maybe_Sim_RenderFrame, Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets, Gau_RovingGunsightWidget, Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator, ~90 more sites) but never seen holding the HB0/HB2 background bitmap itself -- that field, and the exact function that blits the cockpit background art and composites the live 3D view into it, were not pinned to a specific offset/address this session (see docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md's open items). NOT the same object as maybe_MechInspectViewInstance (DAT_004d2544), a separate, much smaller (0x37-byte) object built by Sim_InitMissionSession right after this singleton is already in use.

entries.name: maybe_Sim_RenderFrame
entries.description: Confirmed per-frame ordering relevant to cockpit/HUD compositing (Milestone 8 Phase 0): Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion, then FUN_004327ac(CockpitViewInstance) (per-widget paint dispatch over the weapon-slot array and chain/link/autotrack/shield/etc. sub-widgets), then maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects (the 3D world), then Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, then three more vtable paint dispatches on CockpitViewInstance sub-objects (+0x1f5, FUN_00433158's result, +0x20b). Widget paint therefore happens BEFORE the 3D scene submit each frame, not after -- relevant to how Phase 2/3's Overlay2DRenderer should order its own draw calls relative to SceneRenderer, though DBSIM's own software-blit ordering doesn't have to constrain an OpenGL implementation that composites via alpha/depth instead.
entries.source: docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md 2026-08-15 (Milestone 8 Phase 0); confidence/name unchanged from docs/formats/terrain-texturing.md 2026-08-13

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Ctor
entries.description: CORRECTS the earlier 'MechInspectView' hypothesis. This 0x37-byte object IS the player's own cockpit view manager (MECHVIEW.CPP): it holds the current view index at +0x14, the pending view command at +0x18, the CockpitView widget tree pointer at +0x1f, the owning mech at +0x29 and the herc model name at +0x2d, and it is what CockpitView_SetView/CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand drive. It is small because the heavy state lives in the CockpitView object it builds (see CockpitViewManager_LoadViews -> FUN_00431008 -> CockpitViewInstance). Also the site of CockpitPaletteSingleton's first (singleton-guarded) load of dpl\\cockpit.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_LoadViews
entries.description: The whole cockpit bring-up, in order: (1) loads vue\\<herc> -- int32 viewCount then viewCount x 32-byte records {int x0,y0,x1,y1, cx, cy, canvasOriginX, canvasOriginY}, all coordinates shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift; every retail .VUE has viewCount=4; (2) allocates 4 slots for canopy bitmaps, 4 x 0x204 clip-region blocks and 4 span tables; (3) per view i, calls CockpitClipRegions_Load on ed<i>/hd<i> and ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans on the result, and (unless CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand) CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap for db<i>/hb<i>; (4) builds the CockpitView widget object (FUN_00431008 -> ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, which sets CockpitViewInstance) and Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets; (5) THE PER-HERC COCKPIT COLOUR SCHEME: Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, COCKPIT.DPL.entries + (schemeIdx*0x18 + 0x20)*4), i.e. live palette slots 42..65 are overwritten with COCKPIT.DPL entries [32 + 24*schemeIdx .. +24), where schemeIdx = mechTypeRecord+0x52 = offset 80 of simvol0/dat/<MECH>.DAT (HercSimDat.Unk80_ValHudId). Retail values are a 0-8 permutation: APOCA 0, COLOSSUS 1, SAMSON 2, MAVERICK 3, OGRE 4, OUTLAW 5, RAPTOR2 6, RAZOR 7, TOMAHAWK 8, so the nine 24-entry schemes fill COCKPIT.DPL entries 32..247. This matches the independently measured retail screenshots exactly (APOCA renders canopy index i as COCKPIT.DPL[i-10] => base 32; COLOSSUS as COCKPIT.DPL[i+14] => base 56) and explains why every WORLD<n>.DPL parks exactly slots 42-65 at filler green. (6) Repeats the same install with IMPACTCP.DPL into the secondary palette object DAT_0049aef8 for the damage flash.

entries.name: CockpitViewManagerInstance
entries.description: Result of CockpitViewManager_Ctor, constructed in Sim_InitMissionSession. The player's cockpit view-state object (current view, pending view command, the 4 canopy bitmaps / clip blocks / span tables, and the CockpitView widget tree). Distinct from, and the owner of, CockpitViewInstance (DAT_0049b088).

entries.name: Resource_Load
entries.description: Resource_Load(path): wraps a folder\name string into a temporary object and calls ClassItem_LoadResource(obj, 0), returning the loaded resource handle. The single entry point every HUD sprite bank, panel and cursor load goes through after ResourcePath_BuildFolderName builds the path.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges
entries.description: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges(from, to, rampCount, levels, out): linearly interpolates palette index RANGES, not colours. Each of from/to/out is an array of (int16 start, int16 count) pairs; for each of rampCount ramps it emits `levels` interpolated ranges in 8.8 fixed point, with the final step forced exactly to the `to` endpoint. Called twice by maybe_World_LoadTheater with endpoint tables read from WORLD<n>.WLD. WORLD0 expands to 11 ramps x 16 levels, all ranges within indices 96-239 (terrain shading only; no cockpit equivalent found).

entries.name: Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges
entries.description: Per-frame animated palette cycling. Walks 5 fixed slots (DAT_004cfde8 descriptors, DAT_004cfdfc next-due times, DAT_004cfe10 rotation offsets); when a slot's due time passes it rotates that slot's palette sub-range by one entry and reinstalls it via Palette_InstallRange. Keyed off Time_GetCoarseTicks. Blinking cockpit/console lights.

OPEN LEAD for the unresolved cockpit canopy shading. Copies the live 256-entry palette into two scratch buffers, halves the RGB of two 16-entry spans, and installs them via Palette_InstallRange at base 0x20 (32) and base 0x40 (64) -- both inside the canopy art's own 42-71 index band. Candidate for the lighting-state mechanism that CockpitArt.PaletteIndexOffset currently stands in for. Callers not yet traced.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the HUD heading tick tape. Lazily loads the `hudhtick` sprite bank into DAT_0049be70, selecting folder "hba" or "dba" off DAT_004d25f0 (the 640-wide vs 320-wide video mode flag).

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the multi-function display. Lazily loads three sprite banks -- `mfd` (DAT_0049cbcc), `mfd_dmg` (DAT_0049cbd4) and `radar` -- each selecting folder "hba"/"dba" off DAT_004d25f0.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for a weapon hardpoint gauge. Lazily loads the `pweapons` (DAT_0049c4d0) and `wpn_dmg` (DAT_0049c4d4) sprite banks, folder selected off DAT_004d25f0, and builds a 2-row animation frame table into _DAT_004d1adc.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the throttle slider gauge. Lazily loads the `throttle` sprite bank into DAT_0049cfc4, folder selected by DAT_004d25bb == 3 choosing "hba" over "dba". Reads CockpitViewInstance and its own .GAU track rect. Bank frame 0 is a 2px tick, frame 1 the knob.

entries.name: maybe_SysButtonPair_Ctor
entries.description: Lazily loads the `sysbuttn` sprite bank into DAT_0049b63c (folder by DAT_004d25bb == 3), then constructs two widgets whose coordinates are built as `value << (DAT_004d25be & 0x1f)` on X and `<< (DAT_004d25c0 & 0x1f)` on Y -- the per-axis resolution shift that makes .GAU coordinates 320-wide-space and doubles them for 640-wide.

entries.name: maybe_IconGadget_Ctor
entries.description: Lazily loads the `icons` sprite bank into DAT_0049d6b4, folder selected by DAT_004d25bb == 3.

entries.name: maybe_CockpitFontsAndCorners_Init
entries.description: Loads the cockpit's .DFN/.HFN font set (title, cpylw, active, pushed, inactive, green6x8, red6x8) with folder chosen by DAT_004d25bb == 3 selecting "hfn" over "dfn", then the `corners` sprite bank -- hardcoded to "dba", and indeed no hba\CORNERS.HBA exists -- and finally the `alert` bank via the DAT_004d25f0 idiom.

entries.name: HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames
entries.description: HDDGauge frame loader (PHDD.CPP). Builds the resource name `pilot<n>` with _itoa, loads its .OFS animation-offset table (27 entries), then loads the matching sprite bank from folder "dba". Emits the literal errors "HDDGauge::Couldn't load anim offset" / "...bitmap array".

entries.name: VideoMode_UseHiResBanks
entries.description: Nonzero selects the 640-wide `hba` sprite banks, zero selects the 320-wide `dba` ones. Read directly by every HUD bank constructor. A parallel flag DAT_004d25bb == 3 drives the same choice for sysbuttn/throttle/icons and for .hfn over .dfn.

entries.name: VideoMode_XCoordShift
entries.description: Per-axis resolution shift for hardcoded widget coordinates: the exe writes them as `value << (VideoMode_XCoordShift & 0x1f)`. 0 in the 320-wide mode, 1 in the 640-wide one -- the mechanism behind Herculan.Engine's CockpitArt.GauToPixelScale = 2. DAT_004d25c0 is the Y counterpart.

entries.name: VideoMode_YCoordShift
entries.description: Y-axis counterpart of VideoMode_XCoordShift.

entries.name: HudColorTable
entries.description: 27 int16 palette indices, loaded from dat\COLORS.DAT (54-byte payload). HUD data files carry small logical colour ids rather than palette indices; those are resolved through this table once at load time, in place (arr[i] = table[arr[i]]). Read at 16 distinct offsets by ~60 functions; nothing in the image writes the address with an immediate because it is filled from the file. Verified: HDD ids 19/9/15/12 resolve to palette 16/10/13/14 = black/red/yellow/green, matching retail HDD screenshots.

entries.name: HudColorTable_Get
entries.description: Returns HudColorTable[DAT_0049b040[i]] -- resolves a logical colour id held in an initialised id array to a palette index.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_Ctor
entries.description: LEDBarGraph constructor: calls LedBarGraph_CtorBase then installs vtable PTR_FUN_0049bd30.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_CtorBase
entries.description: LedBarGraph_CtorBase(obj, rect, range): precomputes span = (end - start) * 0x10000 / range at field 0x14, start at 0x18, end at 0x1c, and seeds the current fill position at 0x20 from the sign of span -- a negative span fills from the far end back, which is how the H and V variants share one implementation.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_PaintToValue
entries.description: Paints the bar for a 16.16 fixed-point value: fills to start + (value * span >> 16) via LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe, then installs field 0x24 as the draw colour and covers the remainder.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe
entries.description: Fills the lit span of an LED bar. Walks the x range twice -- once over even columns, once over odd -- drawing a full-height line each step, with field 0x2c as the even-column colour and 0x30 as the odd. Two near-identical shades interleaved at one pixel read as a single shaded fill rather than two colours.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The real shield meter, called only by Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget (00432454) with .GAU offset 0x268=616. NOT an LED bar -- it loads no sprite bank and instead builds a 0x40-byte child per shield facing via FUN_00444aec plus a text label via FUN_004387ac/FUN_00438884 (the same generic label constructors the .DFN font consumers use). That matches retail: nested green concentric boxes with a numeric readout above and below. The .GAU block at 616 is a zero header rect followed by four 16-byte rects at 632/648/664/680, all shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift in FUN_00444b9c. Distinct from EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor (00444d5c), which the earlier maybe_ShieldsGauge_Ctor name wrongly claimed was this widget.

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor
entries.description: CORRECTS the earlier maybe_ShieldsGauge_Ctor name. This is the Master Energy Pool meter (reactor charge), not the shield meter. Called only by Gau_EnergyMeterWidget (004323e0) with .GAU offset 0x224=548, whose child rect is at 564 -- in OUTLAW.GAU that rect is (91,198)-(115,205), directly under the TRACK button, which is where retail draws the blue pinstripe bar. Builds an LED bar with value range 0x400, writing HudColorTable ids 6 and 5 into the pinstripe colour fields 0x2c/0x30 and id 19 into the remainder colour 0x24; against the corrected palette those resolve to palette indices 98/97/16 = (0,116,204), (0,40,160), (0,0,0), i.e. blue -- the old note's 'ids resolve to two greys and black' was computed against the superseded palette model. Class identity is from the binary's own class-name table, which pairs 'EnergyPoolGauge' immediately with 'LEDBarGraphV' (file offset 280429) and 'ShieldsGauge' with 'ShieldsSelectGadget' (279148): the LED bar class is EnergyPoolGauge, and ShieldsGauge is a different class entirely (see ShieldsGauge_Ctor).

entries.name: PaperDoll_Load
entries.description: pdamage.cpp .PDG loader. Reads 3 views, each an origin/size pair plus a vector of 0x1c-byte regions {int index, PixelPoint topLeft, PixelPoint bottomRight, int colorId, int spacer}; resolves each region's colorId through HudColorTable in place and shifts its coordinates by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift, with bottomRight additionally +1 in the 640-wide mode. Matches HercWorks.Core's PaperDollGraphic field-for-field, identifying its ViewRegion.Unk_val at offset 0x14 as the colour id.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap
entries.description: MECHVIEW.CPP:0x12e. THE previously-unlocated .HB0/.HB1/.HB2 (.DB0/.DB1/.DB2) load site. No literal 'hb0' string exists because the folder name is built at runtime: it copies the global folder literal 'dba' (or 'hba' when VideoMode_UseHiResPanels==3) into a stack buffer and overwrites index 2 with an ASCII digit via _itoa, giving db0/db1/db2 or hb0/hb1/hb2, then ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, buf) + ClassItem_LoadResource. View->file map: fileIdx = viewIdx>2 ? viewIdx-1 : viewIdx, so views 0,1,2,3 -> files 0,1,2,2 and view 4 loads nothing; after loading file 2 the same handle is also stored in slot 3, i.e. views 2 and 3 share one bitmap (view 3 is drawn horizontally mirrored, see CockpitView_SetView). Result handles land in CockpitViewManager+8[viewIdx]. The CockpitLayoutMode==1 branch increments byte 2 of the SHARED global 'dba' literal (MOV ECX,[0x4a0a28]; INC byte ptr [ECX+2]) rather than the local buffer -- verified in raw disassembly at 00429d3e; the follow-on load still uses the unmodified local buffer, so that branch loads db0 twice and corrupts the global folder name. Treat CockpitLayoutMode==1 as an unused/buggy path.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_FreeViewBitmap
entries.description: Releases the canopy bitmap handle for one view and nulls its slot; when freeing view 2 it also nulls slot 3, which shares the same handle. Only called when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand (DAT_004d2704) is set, i.e. the low-memory mode that loads and frees canopy art per view switch instead of keeping all four resident.

entries.name: CockpitView_ApplyViewState
entries.description: Installs one view's state into the global render context (DAT_006c5ff4): copies that view's 0x204-byte clip-region block (CockpitViewManager+0xc + viewIdx*0x204, filled by CockpitClipRegions_Load) into ctx+4..ctx+0x208, points ActiveScanlineClipSpans at the view's prebuilt per-scanline span table (CockpitViewManager+0x10[viewIdx]), and copies the view's six .VUE ints into ctx[0x84..0x89]. The .VUE record's last two ints are the view's origin inside the cockpit canvas and go to DAT_004cfa24/28 (or VideoMode_X/YCoordShift-space DAT_004d25da/de in CockpitLayoutMode 2). View 4 instead installs the default full-screen clip block at DAT_004cfb1c and hides the cockpit widgets -- it is the external/no-cockpit view.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetView
entries.description: Switches the cockpit to view 0-4. Calls CockpitView_ApplyViewState, then blits the view's full-screen canopy bitmap once via Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {0,0}, flags) with flags = 2 (horizontal mirror) for view 3 and 0 otherwise -- this is where the side view's single authored bitmap is flipped for the opposite side. Finally repaints every cockpit widget (FUN_004316c0). The canopy is NOT redrawn per frame: it is blitted once per view change and the 3D scene is then rasterized over it, clipped to ActiveScanlineClipSpans. In CockpitLayoutMode 1 view 0 additionally blits slot 1 at y+0xc5.

entries.name: CockpitView_QueueViewCommand
entries.description: Latches a pending view-change command (field +0x18) from an input action, guarded by the current view (field +0x14). Consumed by CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand.

entries.name: CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand
entries.description: Executes the pending view command. Command 4 selects view 2 and adds -0x3600 to the pilot view yaw; command 5 selects view 3 and adds +0x3600; command 6 returns to view 0 and undoes the yaw. 0x3600/0x10000 of a turn = ~76 degrees, i.e. views 2 and 3 are the two 'glance sideways' views. Command 2 selects view 4 (external).

entries.name: CockpitClipRegions_Load
entries.description: Parser for the per-view .ED0-.ED3 / .HD0-.HD3 files (folder name built by overwriting index 2 of the 'edg'/'hdg' literals with a digit). Layout after the 9-byte VOL prefix: int16 rectCount, rectCount x {int16 y0, y1, x0, x1}; then int16 spanBlockCount, and per block {int16 firstRow, int16 rowCount, rowCount x {int16 xStart, int16 xEnd}}. Rects become type-0 region objects, span blocks type-2. Coordinates are shifted by the caller's (xShift,yShift) pair, which is (0,0) for the .HD* hi-res set and VideoMode_X/YCoordShift for the .DB*-era .ED* set. Output is a 0x204-byte block (int count + up to 128 region pointers). APOCA.HD0 reads cleanly: one full-width rect for rows 0-76 then a 235-row span block from row 77 whose spans narrow inward (the canopy frame). APOCA.HD1 is empty (rectCount=0, blockCount=0), which is why view 1 shows no 3D at all.

entries.name: ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans
entries.description: Flattens a loaded region list (rects + span blocks from CockpitClipRegions_Load) into a per-scanline span table of `rowCount` rows (0xf0 << VideoMode_YCoordShift, i.e. 240 or 480). Each row is {int spanCount, ptr to spanCount x {int start, int length}}, sorted by start. Stores the result in ActiveScanlineClipSpans. This -- not any colour key -- is the cockpit's 3D-viewport cutout mechanism.

entries.name: ActiveScanlineClipSpans
entries.description: Pointer to the current view's per-scanline visible-span table (built by ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans). The polygon rasterizer at 00468310 indexes it per row (row*8 -> {spanCount, spanPtr}) and skips rows whose span count is zero, so the 3D scene only ever paints through the canopy's cut-out. Set to 0 for view 4 (no cockpit, unclipped full screen).

entries.name: Bitmap_Blit
entries.description: Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {int x, int y}, flags) -- the engine-wide sprite/background blit. flags bit 1 (value 2) mirrors horizontally, bit 0 (value 1) flips vertically, 3 does both; confirmed at the reticle corner-bracket draw (0044401d..0044403a) which draws one corner sprite four times with flags 0/2/1/3, offsetting x by the bitmap's width field (+6) for flag 2 and y by its height field (+4) for flag 1. Used with flags=2 to produce the cockpit's opposite side view from the single authored side bitmap.

entries.name: Palette_LoadAndActivate
entries.description: Loads a .DPL by path and makes it THE active palette object (ActivePaletteObject / DAT_0049b020). World_LoadTheater calls it with dpl\\world<N>, so the live 256-slot palette IS the theater palette in its entirety -- it is not a merge of COCKPIT.DPL and WORLD<N>.DPL. The only cockpit-owned slots are 42..65, overwritten afterwards by the per-herc scheme install in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews.

entries.name: Palette_SetActive
entries.description: Swaps ActivePaletteObject and returns the previous one. Used to temporarily retarget Palette_InstallRange at the secondary impact palette (DAT_0049aef8) without disturbing the live one.

entries.name: Palette_FlushDirtyRange
entries.description: Pushes the accumulated dirty index range to the display and clears it; if the active palette object changed since the last flush it uploads the whole palette instead.

entries.name: Palette_BeginCrossFade
entries.description: Palette_BeginCrossFade(fromPalette, toPalette, durationTicks): precomputes per-channel 8.8 deltas into DAT_004cfe28/004d0028/004d0228 for a timed fade between two palette objects (either endpoint may be null, meaning fade to/from black). Driven per frame by Palette_StepCrossFade. This is how the impact/damage flash is applied on top of the cockpit's own colour scheme.

entries.name: Palette_StepCrossFade
entries.description: Advances the Palette_BeginCrossFade fade one frame, writing interpolated RGB straight into the live palette and extending the dirty range. Returns remaining ticks, 0 when finished.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateColours
entries.description: Colour-space sibling of Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges: interpolates rampCount colour pairs across `levels` steps, emitting 0x01RRGGBB-style entries. Distinct from the index-range remapper used for terrain shading.

entries.name: ActivePaletteObject
entries.description: The live palette object. Field +8 is its 256 x 4-byte entry array (the array every Palette_* helper indexes). Installed by Palette_LoadAndActivate from dpl\\world<N>; DAT_0049b028/0x2c/0x30 are its dirty min/max/valid triple and DAT_0049b024 the last-uploaded object.

entries.name: VideoMode_Configure
entries.description: Sets the whole video-mode global block from a mode byte read out of the prefs file. Mode 0: VideoMode_UseHiResPanels=0, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 320x240, canvas 320x480, coord shifts 0. Mode 1: UseHiResPanels=3, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 640x480, canvas 640x960, shifts 1. Mode 2: as mode 1 but UseHiResBanks=1. So UseHiResPanels==3 selects .HFN/.HBA/.HB<n> art while UseHiResBanks separately selects the hi-res HUD sprite banks -- which is why the two idioms documented in cockpit-hud.md differ.

entries.name: VideoMode_UseHiResPanels
entries.description: 0 or 3. When 3 the engine loads the 640-wide art set: .HFN fonts, hba\\ sprite banks, and the hb0/hb1/hb2 canopy folders (via CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap) plus the hd0-hd3 clip files. Set by VideoMode_Configure.

entries.name: maybe_CockpitLayoutMode
entries.description: Alternate cockpit layout selector, 0 by default. Value 1 makes view 0 also blit the view-1 (heads-down) bitmap at y+0xc5 and disables view 1 as a standalone view -- but its second load reuses the unmodified local folder buffer and corrupts the global 'dba' literal, so it looks like dead/buggy code. Value 2 routes blits through the windowed variant (Bitmap_BlitClipped) and moves the view origin into DAT_004d25da/de. Never observed written anywhere in the image.

entries.name: CockpitCanvasWidth
entries.description: Width of the virtual cockpit canvas the .GAU widget rects are authored in: 320 in mode 0, 640 in modes 1/2 (paired with CockpitCanvasHeight at 004d25d6 = 480 / 960). The canvas is TALLER than the 3D viewport (004d25c2/c6 = 320x240 / 640x480) because view 1's .VUE origin is (0,237): canvas rows 0-239 are the forward cockpit and rows 237-476 are the heads-down display. Views 2 and 3 sit at canvas x +320 and -320. This is why .GAU's addressable Y range runs past 240.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor
entries.description: Builds one 0x40-byte shield-facing child for ShieldsGauge_Ctor, one per facing, over the .GAU rects at 632 and 648. Draws no geometry: its paint slot (FUN_00444b5c) only tests visibility. The nested concentric rings the retail meter shows are painted into the herc's own canopy art in palette indices 66-71; the gauge animates them by rewriting those six palette slots (ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette).

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette
entries.description: Computes the shield meter's six ring colours and installs them at palette index 0x42 (66-71). Per facing (charge at +0xb5 and +0xb9) three rings light in turn: ring 1 from 0, ring 2 from 0x100 at twice the rate, ring 3 from 0x180 at four times, each as base * t >> 10 in Q10. Above 0x400 the same three tracks run again over base + (bright - base) * t. Colour immediates at 0049c9cb..0049c9d0: base RGB6 (25,59,23), bright (59,59,23). Install order is the stack layout, so 66-68 are the first facing outermost-first and 69-71 the second. At the nominal half charge all six resolve to RGB (48,116,44), matching the retail screenshot's meter.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts
entries.description: Fills ShieldsGauge's two numeric labels (object +0xc4 and +0xc8) from the fore/aft balance at +0xbd: itoa(balance * 200 >> 10) and its complement out of 200. An even split reads 100 and 100, which is what retail shows.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: One weapon row's select gadget, built by FUN_00440a68 from the .GAU hardpoint rect. Lays out two sub-rects relative to that rect, mirrored from the right edge for a right-column slot: the hardpoint state box at +6..+9 GAU x, +0..+7 y (PWEAPONS frames 4-6, 6x14 device), and the weapon-name label at +11..+35 x, +0..+5 y. Painted by WeaponSelectGadget_Paint.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Paint
entries.description: Paints one weapon row: the row plate from PWEAPONS frame 0 (selected) or 1 (not) at the .GAU rect minus one device pixel on both axes, the hardpoint state box from PWEAPONS frames 4/5/6 by state, the weapon name from the gauge's own 12-char buffer (+0xb1), and the round count. Text colour is the font: ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE / [11] GRAY for the name, [13] GREEN / [11] GRAY for the count; the label's field 0x1d is the background colour it paints first (0x2e here).

entries.name: ConsoleButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints the chain/link/auto-track console buttons: plate from PWEAPONS frames 2 + state (frame 2 unlit, solid palette index 34 = the retail blue at RGB (77,77,182); frame 3 lit, index 14 green) blitted at the widget's own rect, then the caption. The chain button's caption comes from the three-entry Roman-numeral table at 0049c71c ('I', 'II', 'III'), a literal .rdata table unrelated to the string file. LINK and TRACK are not fixed the same way: both read ConsoleButtonCaptions (004d13d0) indexed by the widget's own kind field (param_1[10]: 1=LINK, 2=TRACK), which SimStrings_LoadAll fills from STRINGS0.STR group 4. Caption font is ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when unlit, [12] DARK when lit.

entries.name: ChainCountCaptions
entries.description: Three 4-byte inline strings 'I', 'II', 'III' indexed by chain count, read by ConsoleButton_Paint.

entries.name: ConsoleButtonCaptions
entries.description: 4-entry .bss pointer array (STRINGS0.STR group 4: 'I', 'LINK', 'TRACK', ''), filled by SimStrings_LoadAll and read by ConsoleButton_Paint, indexed by the console button's own kind field. Entry 0 ('I') is unused by that reader -- the chain button gets its numerals from the separate ChainCountCaptions table instead.

entries.name: ShieldRingColors
entries.description: Six bytes of 6-bit colour channels for the shield meter's ring ramp: base R,G,B at +0..+2 = (25,59,23) and bright R,G,B at +3..+5 = (59,59,23). Read only by ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette. Channel order matches the .DPL entry layout, byte 0 = R.

entries.name: CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand
entries.description: When non-zero, canopy view bitmaps are loaded on entering a view and freed on leaving it instead of all being loaded up front in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews. A low-memory path.

entries.name: MfdGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Coordinate-shifts the MFD's .GAU block at offset 728 in place before MfdDisplay_Ctor reads it: 13 consecutive rects from int index 4 (file offset 744), then the panel rect at int index 0x38 (file offset 952). The 13 rects are zero in all nine retail .GAU files and no constructor reads them; only the panel rect is live. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetMode
entries.description: Switches the MFD to a screen (0-5, = F-key - 1). Lights button `mode` and unlights the previous via their +0x40 flag, stores the mode at +0xc1, then walks the 6x13 visibility table at 0049cbd8 for buttons 6-12 showing/hiding each. Gau_MfdPanelWidget calls it with 3 (SCANNER) at build time, which is what a cockpit powers up on. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Full MFD repaint, in order: mode buttons 0-5, the screen background, all visible buttons 0-12, the current screen's paint slot, then the title from DAT_004d13e0[mode]. Background frame is a bare switch on the mode over the `mfd` bank's frame-pointer array: modes 0/1/4 take element 1, mode 3 element 2, modes 2/5 take literal 0 and skip the blit. Frame 0 is never used as a background. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Update
entries.description: MFD per-frame update. Dispatches the current screen's update slot via +0xcd + mode*4, refreshes the title for modes 2 and 5, and when a transmission is active draws the speaking pilot's frames at inset+(0x14,0) and fills the message label at +0x329. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_OnClick
entries.description: MFD button dispatch: finds the clicked button's index in the +0x18 array, then switches on it. Indices 0-5 call MfdDisplay_SetMode(i) -- this is what makes mode index = F-key - 1. Index 11 (PASS) and 12 (ACTIVE) set the radar-mode flag at CockpitViewInstance+0x203's +0x96 to 0/1 and swap which of the two lights. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_SetCaption
entries.description: Sets one MFD button's caption from its index at +0x28: for index < 6 it composes "F1"-"F6" on the stack from the two-byte literal at 0049cea3 ("Fx") with '1'+index written over the second byte -- the six mode captions are not stored as strings. For index >= 6 it takes DAT_004d13e0[index] from STRINGS0.STR group 5. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_Repaint
entries.description: Repaints one MFD button and re-fonts its caption: buttons 0-5 and 11-12 take ColorSchemePanels[12] DARK when the +0x40 lit flag is set and [10] WHITE when clear, which is why the selected F-key reads dark-on-green. Caption text is resolved the same way as MfdButton_SetCaption. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's FLASH COMM screen (mode 1). Builds six order rows: rect inset+(2,0xd)-(0x60,0x3a) GAU with the top-left nudged in and bottom-right out by 1<<XCoordShift, stepping 7<<YCoordShift per row. Font ColorSchemePanels[1] CPGREEN with [2] CPRED as the alternate at +0x21, background colour id 0x11, text margin 2<<XCoordShift. Rows list the first six of STRINGS0.STR group 0's 18 squadmate orders. See docs/formats/mfd.md.
