entries.name: MfdMapScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's NAV MAP screen (mode 2). Takes the whole inset rect, allocates a 0x239-byte offscreen render target and centres it at -((x1-x0)>>1), -((y1-y0)>>1). No labels and no aux buttons. Its paint (004405e4) floods the rect with COLORS.DAT id 19 (black) before rasterizing terrain, which is why MfdDisplay_Repaint blits no chrome for this mode. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's SCANNER screen (mode 3), the largest of the six at 0x524 bytes. Owns the contact list and the `radar` bank's 10-frame 110x110 sweep animation. Range comes from _DAT_004d1cf4 = 50000/100000/200000 world units (300/600/1200 m at 1000 units = 6 m) indexed by the zoom field at MfdDisplay+0xc5, default 2. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's MISSILE CAM screen (mode 5), matching the MFDMissileView class name in DBSIM's string table. Like the nav map it gets no background chrome from MfdDisplay_Repaint, filling the screen with its own camera image. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Label_SetRect
entries.description: Anchors a HUD text label: stores the caller's rect at label+1..4 and computes the text anchor. Horizontal depends on the flags argument -- 2 = centre ((x1-x0)/2 + x0 + margin[0]), 4 = right (x1 - margin[0]), otherwise left (x0 + margin[0]). Vertical has no flag at all: anchorY = ((y1-y0)>>1) + y0 + (inkHeight>>1) + margin[2] + 1, where inkHeight is font+0x16 (file offset 0x1a, 11 for .HFN) and NOT the cell height at font+0xa. All of it is integer arithmetic. margin is the caller's short[4]. Paired with Label_SetText. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Label_SetText
entries.description: Sets a HUD label's text and places it against the anchor Label_SetRect computed. Measures the run and subtracts 1<<XCoordShift (dropping the trailing advance), then places left/centre/right per the same flags. Vertical position is the stored anchor; HudFont_DrawGlyph then draws each glyph with its top row at anchor - inkHeight, so the inked band is what gets centred in the rect and the remaining cell rows hang below. Fills the label's background first when its +0x1d colour id is non-zero. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: SimStrings_LoadAll
entries.description: Opens one str\*.STR file and registers its string groups into .bss pointer arrays, in strict file order -- 41 registrations for STRINGS0.STR, so a group's index is its position in this sequence. The sixth (13 entries into DAT_004d13e0) is the MFD's caption/title table. A registration passes a second destination array only for groups whose entries carry attribute bytes, which matches the file's own self-describing per-entry attribute count. See docs/formats/str-strings.md.

entries.name: MfdCaptionTable
entries.description: 13 pointers into STRINGS0.STR group 5, filled at runtime by SimStrings_LoadAll (BSS, zero in the image). Entries 0-5 are the MFD's six screen titles (STATUS, FLASH COMM, NAV MAP, SCANNER, TARGET, MISSILE CAM) and 6-12 its aux button captions (MODE, SELECT, RANGE, TARGET, XMIT, PASS, ACTIVE). Indexed by mode for the title and by button index for captions. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButtonRects
entries.description: Four parallel int16[13] tables giving the MFD's button rects in GAU units relative to the inset screen origin: 0049cacc x0, 0049cae6 y0, 0049cb00 x1, 0049cb1a y1. Indices 0-5 are the F-key mode column at x -16..-2 with a 10-unit pitch (negative because the column sits left of the inset), 6 is a degenerate zero rect, 7-12 the per-screen aux buttons. Every rect size matches a dba\MFD.DBA frame size exactly. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButtonVisibility
entries.description: 6 rows x 13 bytes: which buttons each MFD mode shows. Indices 0-5 are 1 in every row; the aux columns give SELECT on modes 0 and 4, XMIT on 1, RANGE/TARGET/PASS/ACTIVE on 3, and none on 2 and 5. MfdDisplay_SetMode and MfdDisplay_Repaint address it as &table[mode][6], which the decompiler folds into DAT_0049cbde + mode*13. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusLabelTables
entries.description: Three parallel int16[5] tables for the MFD status screen's labels: 0049bd84 x0 (6 for all five), 0049bd8e y0 (16, 23, 32, 40, 49), 0049bd98 font selector (0,1,0,1,1) into {ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE, [14] RED}. All in GAU units relative to the inset screen origin; each label is 6 units tall and runs right to the wireframe viewport's left edge at 45. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition
entries.description: Writes the MFD status screen's fourth and fifth labels. Label 4 (screen+0x1c) takes MfdStatusConditionStrings[state] = STRINGS0.STR group 28; state is the caller's, or FUN_00438700(damage) when the caller passes -1. Label 5 (screen+0x20) is composed from literals: "[ " (0049be2c), itoa((0x100 - damage) * 100 >> 8), then "% ]" (0049be2f) -- undamaged reads "[ 100% ]". When the subject is unreadable (screen+0x34 set) it writes "XXXXXX" and "XXX" instead. NOTE: STRINGS0.STR group 10 holds a near-identical five-string set and is dead data -- SimStrings_LoadAll is the only reference to its array. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusConditionStrings
entries.description: 5 pointers into STRINGS0.STR group 28 -- OK, SHIELDS DN, INT DAMAGE, CRITICAL, DESTROYED -- filled at runtime by SimStrings_LoadAll. Indexed by condition state for the MFD status screen's fourth label in MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition. This, not the similar-looking group 10 at DAT_004d1440, is the live table. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdScannerRanges
entries.description: Three int32 scanner ranges -- 50000, 100000, 200000 world units = 300, 600, 1200 m at the game's 1000 units = 6 m scale. Indexed by the MFD's zoom field at +0xc5, which MfdDisplay_Ctor inits to 2; 1200 m matches the RNG: readout in the retail scanner screenshot. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: CockpitView_StepViewTransition
entries.description: Runs a queued view change's animated slide, once per frame from Sim_EndFrame just before CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, gated on pending != -1 and the armed flag at +0x1c. For commands 0/1 (heads-down pan) it steps the display origin y by 10 canvas rows per loop iteration over vue[dest].canvasOriginY - vue[src].canvasOriginY (237, or 474 after the coord shift), then a remainder step; commands 4/5/6 step x by 0x14. The loop has no timer, retrace poll or frame boundary, so its real-time speed is CPU-bound. On completion: +0x14 += 1 (or -1), +0x18 = -1, +0x1d = 2 (two-frame cooldown). See docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md.

entries.name: Sim_EndFrame
entries.description: Per-frame tail: CockpitView_StepViewTransition, Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges, Palette_FlushDirtyRange, page flip (swaps the display context's +0x88/+0x8c page origins through DAT_004a5808/580c), then CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand. The DAT_004d25ea != 0 branch is the hardware-scroll display path.

entries.name: CockpitView_HandleViewKey
entries.description: Maps one pressed key id to a view command by current view. +0x21a is the heads-down key ([F7]/[F8]): view 0 queues command 0 (pan down), view 1 queues command 1 (pan up). +0x21e and +0x222 are the two side-glance keys, queuing 5/4 from view 0 and 6 from views 3/2.

entries.name: CockpitView_PollViewDevice
entries.description: Polls a device-state block for the four view axes -- bytes +0x1e/+0x1f/+0x20/+0x21 queue view commands 1/0/5/4 respectively -- i.e. the joystick hat's up/down/left/right, the alternative to CockpitView_HandleViewKey's keyboard path. Also handles the +0xb button edge.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: HDDisplay constructor, .GAU offset 1212 (PHDD.CPP). Reads the block's origin, four region rects (+0xc1 screen, +0xe1 order column, +0xd1 damage column, +0xf1 title indicator), 15 widget rects and 3 comm-box marker rects; loads the 'static' and 'hdd' sprite banks and the 'hddclip' clip region; builds both page objects (+0x101 command display, +0x105 damage detail), the title label (+0x51b) and three 0x14e-byte comm gauges; ends with HddDisplay_SetPage(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Pre-pass over the .GAU HDD block: adds 0x28 to the origin's y, then shifts every rect in the block by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift. The bias is what turns each retail file's authored origin (0,197) into (0,237), i.e. the same canvas origin the herc's own .VUE gives view 1 -- the row .HB1 is blitted at.

entries.name: HddButton_Ctor
entries.description: One HDDisplay sub-widget: rect at [0..3], owning display at param_1[9], index at param_1[10], label at param_1[0xb], unlit/lit frames at param_1[0xc]/[0xd], visibility state at +0x1b (2 = hidden), lit flag at +0x40.

entries.name: HddButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints one HDDisplay sub-widget, gated on state +0x1b < 2. The frame index differs by case, which is what makes some of these buttons latching and others momentary: indices 0/1 (the F7/F8 page buttons) take the frame from the object's own selection flag +0x40 and caption themselves 'F7'/'F8' from the shared 'Fx' literal at 0049d4f5 in ColorSchemePanels[12] selected / [10] not -- they have no pressed state; 2-7 (four arrows, two map magnifiers) take the frame from the shared press byte +0x1b and so light only while held; 10-12 fill the selected comm box's marker rect; 13/14 blit the plate and caption XMIT/CANCEL from STRINGS0 group 9, both frame and font indexed by that same press byte (ColorSchemePanels[4 + pressed]).

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetPage
entries.description: Switches the display between its two pages (0 = command display [F7], 1 = damage detail [F8]): unlights the old page button, hides the old page object, shows the new one, lights its button, then applies the 2x15 widget visibility table at HddPageWidgetVisibility -- a 0 sets the widget's state to 2, the value HddButton_Paint refuses to draw at.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetTitle
entries.description: Fills the title label (+0x51b) from STRINGS0 group 11 entry 0 ('MAP') on page 0, or group 12 indexed by the damage screen's current category (' STRUCT DAMAGE' / ' INTERN DAMAGE' / ' WEAPON DAMAGE') on page 1.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SelectPilot
entries.description: Selects one of the three squad comm boxes (widgets 10-12): unlights the previous, records it at +0x52b, stores the new index at +0x517, lights its widget, sends the pilot a select message, and tells the command screen.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Whole-display paint: every visible widget, then the current page object's paint, then the title indicator rect (+0xf1, colour id 13 or -- while +0x51f is set, which the constructor does -- id 15), then HddDisplay_SetTitle, then the three comm gauges. A gauge slot with no squadmate in it is flooded with colour id 19 inset one device pixel instead.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Ctor
entries.description: The [F7] command display. Builds the map viewport as the screen rect inset (4<<XCoordShift, 2<<YCoordShift) with its right edge at the order column's left minus the same, a 0x239-byte offscreen map render target centred on the zone, 140 map marker gadgets, and nine label rows down the order column at (y1-y0)/9 pitch: row 0 the incoming-message label in ColorSchemePanels[2], rows 1-8 the orders in [1] with [2] as the hotkey alternate.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Repaint
entries.description: Floods the screen rect with colour id 19, refreshes the order rows, draws the selected order's 2px marker bar in id 15, repaints the two magnifier buttons, rebuilds the map markers and rasterizes the map.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_RefreshOrders
entries.description: Re-fonts and re-texts the eight order rows from STRINGS0 group 0 entries 10-17, passing each entry's single attribute byte as the index of its hotkey character within its own text. An available order draws in ColorSchemePanels[1] CPGREEN with the hotkey in [2] CPRED, an unavailable one wholly in [0] CPBLUE, and the selected one in [3] CPYLW.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawOrderHighlight
entries.description: Blits HDD bank frame 2 + state (or 4) -- the 116x18 selected-order bar -- at an order label's own text position.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_BuildMapMarkers
entries.description: Rebuilds the map's marker gadgets: up to 9 waypoint markers from the player's own route (icons 0x4e+), then one per object in the three global object lists, then the player's own marker (icon 0x57). Gadgets past the last used one, out of the 140 allocated, are released.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Ctor
entries.description: The [F8] damage detail. Resolves its four colour ids at HddDamageColorIds through HudColorTable in place, then builds 13 rows of two labels each down the damage column: a name from the column's left edge + 0x1e<<XCoordShift, and a value column whose width is the measured width of the literal '100'. Rows are 4<<YCoordShift tall at 7<<YCoordShift pitch, all in ColorSchemePanels[1] on colour id 19. Also builds the subject caption at the screen's bottom-left and a centred no-data label, then calls HddDamageScreen_SetView(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_SetView
entries.description: Selects the damage category and its row count: 0 structural = 0x13 rows, 1 internal = 0xc, 2 weapons = the subject's own fitted weapon count. The manual binds these to [S], [I] and [W], and to the display's up/down arrow buttons.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Update
entries.description: Per-frame update and repaint. Picks the name table by category and subject type -- STRINGS0 groups 13/14 for structural (walker/flyer), 15/16 for internal, the mech's own weapon names for weapons -- floods the screen with colour id 3, sets the subject caption, blits the .PDG view for the category (0 structural, 1 internal) at the screen rect's top-left plus the view's own origin, tints its regions, and refills the rows.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_SetSubjectCaption
entries.description: Sets the damage screen's subject caption from the display's five-entry name array at +0x548 (the player's 'YOU', three squadmate names, then 'TARGET') indexed by the subject selector at +0x55c. The player draws in ColorSchemePanels[3] on colour id 6, a squadmate in [2] on that pilot's own COLORS.DAT entry, and the target in [2] on id 15.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintIdle
entries.description: Paints one squad comm box while its pilot is not broadcasting: floods the video area with colour id 19 and fills five labels -- the pilot's name, 'STATUS:', the condition from STRINGS0 group 28, 'OBJECTIVE:', and the pilot's current order from group 40. Matches the manual's 'their video box remains darkened, displaying only their name, their status, and their current orders'. Defers to HddGauge_PaintStatic when the pilot's comms are out.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintStatic
entries.description: Draws the next of the 'static' bank's five frames into a comm box and advances the cycle -- the manual's 'the video box goes to static and you can send them no messages'.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame
entries.description: Draws one frame of a talking pilot into a comm box: floods it with colour id 19, blits the requested frame of the pilot<n> bank at that frame's own .OFS offset pair, and refreshes the name label.

entries.name: HddGauge_ConditionIndex
entries.description: Averages a mech's 19 structural damage bytes into a 0-100 integrity percentage and buckets it into the five STRINGS0 group 28 conditions at 90 / 74 / 51 / 1 -- OK, SHIELDS DN, INT DAMAGE, CRITICAL, DESTROYED.

entries.name: HddPageWidgetVisibility
entries.description: 2 rows x 15 bytes, indexed [page][widget] by HddDisplay_SetPage. Page 0 shows widgets 0-7 and 13-14, page 1 only 0-5. Both rows hide the three comm boxes (10-12), which HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames re-enables per occupied squad slot.

entries.name: HddSpriteBank
entries.description: The 'hdd' sprite bank handle (hba\HDD.HBA or dba\HDD.DBA), 27 frames: 0-1 the XMIT/CANCEL plate unlit/lit, 2-4 the selected-order highlight bar, 5-12 the first arrow-button set, 13-20 the second, 21-24 the two map magnifiers, 25-26 the F7/F8 page buttons. Which arrow set a herc uses is its own .GAU block value at offset 0x5c.

entries.name: HddStaticBank
entries.description: The 'static' sprite bank handle -- five 64x53 frames of video noise that HddGauge_PaintStatic cycles through a comm box whose pilot's comms are out. Ships in dba\ only.

entries.name: HddDamageColorIds
entries.description: Four COLORS.DAT logical colour ids -- 19, 9, 15, 12 -- that HddDamageScreen_Ctor resolves through HudColorTable in place to palette 16, 10, 13, 14 (black, red, yellow, green) for the damage rows.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawString
entries.description: Draws a NUL-terminated run with a .DFN/.HFN font at a caller-supplied top-left, advancing the pen by each glyph's own width. A display-wide alignment override at renderContext+0x231 (1 = right, 2 = centre against the field width at +0x235) shifts the whole run first; it is 0 in the cockpit.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawGlyph
entries.description: Blits one glyph: height from font+0xa (file 0x0e cellHeight), width from HudFont_GlyphWidth, bit depth from font+0x12 (file 0x16, 8 in every retail file), pixels from the pool at font+0x22 indexed through the per-glyph offset array at font+0x26. Draws with its top row at y - font+0x16 (file 0x1a, the ink height), which is the other half of Label_SetRect's vertical rule.

entries.name: HudFont_GlyphWidth
entries.description: One glyph's advance width: the fixed width at font+0xc when that is not -1, otherwise the per-glyph width byte at font+0x2a indexed by char - firstCharCode. Every retail font stores -1 and is therefore proportional.

entries.name: HudFont_MeasureString
entries.description: Sums HudFont_GlyphWidth over a NUL-terminated run. Callers that align a run subtract 1<<XCoordShift from the result to drop the trailing advance past the last glyph.

entries.name: HudFont_CellHeight
entries.description: Returns font+0xa, the glyph cell height (file offset 0x0e; 13 for .HFN, 10 for .DFN). This is the glyph art's height, not the ink height at font+0x16 that labels centre by.

entries.name: Mouse_WndProcHook
entries.description: Registered into the MainWndProc filter chain (see WndProcHook_Register). Catches WM_MOUSEMOVE(0x200)/WM_LBUTTONDOWN(0x201)/WM_LBUTTONUP(0x202)/WM_RBUTTONDOWN(0x204)/WM_RBUTTONUP(0x205) -- none of which MainWndProc's own switch handles -- and forwards each to Mouse_DispatchEvent with a kind id (0=move,1=ldown,2=lup,3=rdown,4=rup) and a button-held bitmask built from wParam.

entries.name: Mouse_Init
entries.description: Registers Mouse_WndProcHook into the WndProc filter chain and, on first call, resets a clip/extent struct (width 0x140, height 400) via two small copy helpers at 0048062c/00480658 -- purpose not traced further, not needed to understand click handling.

entries.name: Mouse_DispatchEvent
entries.description: Rescales a raw window-client-space (x,y) from Mouse_WndProcHook into the game's internal coordinate space via a fixed-point factor (Mouse_RecomputeScale), packs the current L/R button-held bitmask into DAT_006c5fdc, and calls every enabled entry of the 10-slot mouse-listener table (DAT_006c5f5c, registered via MouseListener_Register) whose event mask has the event kind's bit set.

entries.name: Mouse_RecomputeScale
entries.description: Recomputes DAT_004a2de4/DAT_004a2de8, the 16.15 fixed-point (gameSize<<0xf)/clientSize factors Mouse_DispatchEvent uses to rescale window-client mouse coordinates into game space. Reads the window's current client rect, so it must be re-run on resize.

entries.name: MouseListener_Register
entries.description: Appends {enabled=1, eventMask, callback} to the first free slot (of 10) in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c that Mouse_DispatchEvent fans events out to. Returns the slot index or -1 if full. Same {enabled,mask,fn}-triple-array idiom as WndProcHook_Register's table and the keyboard-binding table read by FUN_00477ae0 -- DBSIM reuses this shape for at least three unrelated subscriber lists.

entries.name: MouseListener_Unregister
entries.description: Clears slot param_2's enabled flag in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Register
entries.description: Appends a raw (hwnd,msg,wParam,lParam)-shaped filter function to the first free slot (of 10) in the table at DAT_004d3bb4 that MainWndProc tries, in order, before its own message switch -- any hook returning nonzero short-circuits MainWndProc entirely. Mouse_WndProcHook is one of four registered hooks found; the others are sound/movie-playback related.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Unregister
entries.description: Removes a hook previously added by WndProcHook_Register from the DAT_004d3bb4 table.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_Init
entries.description: Called once at cockpit setup. Registers CockpitMouse_OnEvent with MouseListener_Register under event mask 0x1e (button down/up on both buttons -- bits 1-4; bit 0, plain movement, is deliberately excluded), allocates the double-buffered per-frame event queue (two Cpp_VectorNew'd 0xe-byte-record vectors, swapped by CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue), and sets the click-vs-drag timing gate DAT_004d1e70 = 0x1e (30 coarse ticks, ~480ms at the ~62.5Hz UI timebase -- the same literal 0x1e as the event mask above but an unrelated field, easy to conflate).

entries.name: CockpitMouse_OnEvent
entries.description: The cockpit's one mouse-listener callback. Does not act on the event synchronously: pushes a {x,y,buttonMask,timestamp} record into the back-buffer queue via CockpitMouseQueue_Push (debounced to once per coarse tick) and, when a software/hardware cursor sprite is active (DAT_0049dbdf), calls Cursor_SyncPosition to keep the drawn pointer following the raw event position immediately rather than waiting for the once-per-frame queue drain.

entries.name: CockpitMouseQueue_Push
entries.description: Appends one 0xe=14-byte record {int32 x, int32 y, uint16 buttonMask, int32 timestamp} to the back-buffer vector at DAT_004d1e88, capped at 99 entries (silently drops further events past that).

entries.name: CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue
entries.description: Swaps the double-buffered event queue and drains it once per frame -- the real click/hover/drag logic. Per record: on a position change, hit-tests via Widget_HitTestChildren and either forwards to the captured widget's drag slot (if mouse-captured) or fires Widget_OnMouseHover; on a button-down edge, calls Widget_OnMouseDown; on a button-up edge, gates on the release landing within DAT_004d1e70 ticks of the press before calling Widget_OnMouseUp (or, if a drag was in progress, ends the capture and fires the captured widget's OnClick/GetValue pair directly).

entries.name: Widget_HitTest
entries.description: Point-in-widget test against a single widget, param_1. A per-widget flag at param_1+0x10 selects the shape: 0 = axis-aligned rect, inclusive bounds at param_1[0..3] (x0,y0,x1,y1); nonzero = circular/diamond region, Manhattan distance from a centre point (param_1+0x11/+0x13, int16 cx,cy) at most a radius (param_1+0x15, int16). The circular form is not exercised by any widget traced so far (MFD/HDD/console buttons and the shield facings are all rectangular); presumably serves a knob/dial-shaped control.

entries.name: Widget_HitTestChildren
entries.description: Linear-scans the flat clickable-widget list at param_1+0x256 (count at +0x254) with Widget_HitTest, returning the index of the first widget under the point whose state (+0x1b) is not 2 (hidden). Not a tree walk: every clickable widget anywhere in the cockpit is registered into one shared list by Widget_RegisterClickable, so an off-screen panel's buttons are excluded purely by their hidden state, not by not being reachable.

entries.name: Widget_OnMouseDown
entries.description: Hit-tests the press position via Widget_HitTestChildren; if a widget is hit, marks its state (+0x1b) pressed (1) and, if that widget opts in via its own +0x1d==1 flag, begins mouse capture (DAT_0049dbde=1) and forwards the position to the widget's drag-move vtable slot. Widgets built with +0x1d left 0 (every button/gauge traced so far) never enter capture and are handled entirely by press/release instead.

entries.name: Widget_OnMouseUp
entries.description: Hit-tests the release position; if it lands on the same widget that was pressed (or the right button is still held), calls the widget's own GetValue then OnClick vtable slots with that value, then clears its pressed state (+0x1b=0) and repaints it via Widget_Repaint. This is where a click actually fires -- CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue only calls this after its own press/release timing gate passes.

entries.name: Widget_TrackPressedWidget
entries.description: On a position change while a button is held, keeps the pressed widget's appearance in sync with the pointer: hit-tests, and if the hit is still the widget in DAT_0049dbdc sets its state (+0x1b) to 1, otherwise clears it to 0, repainting via Widget_Repaint on each change. This is the button that pops back up when you drag off it and depresses again when you return. Guarded entirely on DAT_0049dbdc != -1, and that global is set only by Widget_OnMouseDown and cleared to -1 by Widget_OnMouseUp, so this cannot run unless a button is down. Previously named Widget_OnMouseHover, which was wrong: DBSIM has no hover state, corroborated by CockpitMouse_Init's event mask (0x1e) excluding plain movement.

entries.name: Widget_PressedIndex
entries.description: int16. Index into the cockpit-wide clickable list of the widget a mouse button is currently held down on, or -1 for none. One global for the whole cockpit, not per-panel. Set by Widget_OnMouseDown from its own hit test, read and acted on by Widget_TrackPressedWidget, cleared to -1 at the end of Widget_OnMouseUp. Its -1 guard is what makes Widget_TrackPressedWidget a no-op unless a button is held.

entries.name: Widget_Repaint
entries.description: Calls a widget's own Paint vtable slot after a state change. The slot's numeric offset is not uniform across classes (confirmed +4 for MfdDisplay and HddButton via unambiguous ctor evidence; do not assume the same offset for every class without checking).

entries.name: Widget_RegisterClickable
entries.description: Appends one widget pointer to the caller's flat +0x256 array (count at +0x254) that Widget_HitTestChildren scans. Called once per child during every cockpit widget tree's construction (MfdDisplay_Ctor's 13 MFD buttons, ShieldsGauge_Ctor's 2 facings, etc.) with the *dereferenced* CockpitViewInstance pointer as the shared root -- every clickable widget in the whole cockpit lands in one list, not a per-panel one.

entries.name: Widget_Show
entries.description: Sets the child widget at index param_2 of the caller's +0x256 array to state 0 (normal/visible) and repaints it. Pairs with Widget_Hide.

entries.name: Widget_Hide
entries.description: Sets the child widget at index param_2 of the caller's +0x256 array to state 2 (hidden -- excluded from Widget_HitTestChildren and refused by every traced Paint slot) and repaints it. Pairs with Widget_Show.

entries.name: maybe_Widget_NotifySelfAndChildren
entries.description: Toggles a guard flag (+0x227) around calling vtable slot 0 on the caller itself, then on every widget in its +0x256 clickable-child array. What slot 0 means is class-specific (observed as OnClick/OnCommand for MfdDisplay and ShieldsGauge) so this function's own purpose -- relayout notification, a generic show/refresh cascade -- was not independently confirmed, only its mechanical shape.

entries.name: Cursor_SyncPosition
entries.description: Moves the on-screen pointer to the (x,y) in param_1. If a hardware cursor is active (DAT_004a365e), hides/shows it via two function pointers (DAT_004a5840/DAT_004a583c, a DirectDraw cursor surface's vtable calls) around updating its position (DAT_004a3638/3c); otherwise stashes the position for the software cursor overlay Screen_PresentFrame draws.

entries.name: maybe_Screen_PresentFrame
entries.description: Dual-purpose per-frame presentation: in windowed/GDI mode (_DAT_004d25e2==0), StretchBlt's the backbuffer to the window via BeginPaint/EndPaint; in fullscreen mode, raw-copies the backbuffer into VRAM and, when a software cursor bitmap is active (DAT_004d37a8), blits it at GetCursorPos() clipped to the viewport, colour-keyed on byte value 1. Named for its dominant role (frame presentation); the cursor blit is secondary but confirms the visible pointer is genuinely drawn from the same OS cursor position the click pipeline reads, not a separate abstracted position.

entries.name: maybe_Mouse_WarpCursorToPoint
entries.description: Rescales a game-space point to client coordinates (inverse of Mouse_RecomputeScale's factor) and calls SetCursorPos. Caller(s) and trigger not traced -- plausibly a 'snap cursor to this widget' affordance, not confirmed.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_OnClick
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's own vtable slot 0 (per the same *param_1=&PTR_thisFunction ctor-assignment evidence used for MfdButton_OnClick). Searches its own +0x18/+0x68 child-pointer table (populated identically to MfdDisplay's, by ShieldsGauge_Ctor) for the clicked facing widget; index 0 (front) sets state byte +0xc2=1 clearing +0xc3, index 1 (rear) the reverse. Consumed once per frame by Shield_BalanceInputRead, not painted directly.

entries.name: ShieldFacing_OnClick
entries.description: A shield-facing child widget's own click handler, reached via Widget_OnMouseUp. Gated on the left mouse button bit (param_2&1); forwards the click to its owner (pointer stored at the facing's own +0x24, set to the parent ShieldsGauge at construction) as owner->vtable[0](owner, self, buttonFlags) -- i.e. calls ShieldsGauge_OnClick -- then repaints itself and notifies its label child.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Trivial accessor: returns param_1+0xb5, the start of ShieldsGauge's 15-byte live state block (front charge, rear charge, balance, then the two click flags ShieldsGauge_OnClick sets). Shield_BalanceInputRead copies out of this pointer directly rather than through a richer accessor.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: Write-back counterpart to ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock: overwrites the 15-byte state block at param_1+0xb5 from param_2 (called by Shield_BalanceInputRead with the freshly computed front/rear percentages and a cleared click-flag pair), and sets the dirty flag at +0xb0=2 if the values actually changed. Also zeroes the front/rear fields when the gauge's +0x8d 'shields down' flag is set.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Paint
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's vtable+4 slot. Unconditionally calls ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette and ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Update
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's per-frame update slot (vtable+8, called from the general HUD paint pass, not the click pipeline). Gated on visibility and a 'shields present' flag; when the dirty flag ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock set (+0xb0==2) is pending, refreshes the ring palette and readouts and clears it. This is the bridge between Shield_BalanceInputRead's once-per-frame gameplay update and the HUD paint pass -- the click sets a flag, the gameplay tick consumes it into real sim state and a dirty bit, and this slot is what actually repaints from that bit.

entries.name: ShieldFacing_Paint
entries.description: A shield-facing child's Paint slot. Draws no geometry -- only a visibility test (FUN_00431410) -- because the concentric rings retail shows are palette-animated into the herc's own canopy art, not drawn by this widget (see ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette in docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md).

entries.name: maybe_ShieldFacing_FlashTimer
entries.description: A shield-facing child's update slot: a two-stage counter at +0x1f (2->1 calls FUN_0043122c then decrements; 1->0 just decrements) -- plausibly a brief post-click flash/debounce, not independently confirmed.

entries.name: Sim_PollPlayerInput
entries.description: Reads the input device struct (axes at +0x0e steer, +0x10 throttle, +0x12 torso twist, +0x14 torso pitch) and dispatches player control: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput, Mech_TorsoTwistTick, Mech_TorsoPitchTick. Also hosts the keyboard command switch.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput
entries.description: Player throttle handler. Integrates the stick axis into mech+0x290 (throttle, Q10, clamped +/-0x400) at Q8(0x91,-axis) per tick, converts it to a desired speed via Q10(maxRev or maxFwd, throttle), then calls Mech_LocomotionTick. ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) gates the clamp: at 0 it spans the full +/-0x400, so the axis held down runs through zero into reverse.

entries.name: Mech_LocomotionTick
entries.description: The Herc control law. Sets speed (mech+0x28e), turn rate (mech+0x28c), heading (mech+0x10) and animation rate (mech+0x2a0); about 60 percent of the body is the gait state machine. Writes no position -- all translation is animation root motion. Turn rate is a tent over speed peaking at half top speed; turn-in-place sets only the animation rate.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed
entries.description: Adjusts desired speed by dot(terrainNormal, forwardVector)/0x960, signed by direction of travel, clamped to zero on sign flip. Uphill slows, downhill speeds up.

entries.name: Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance
entries.description: Terrain and obstacle avoidance applied to steering and desired speed. AI only -- Mech_LocomotionTick skips it when the mech is PlayerMech.

entries.name: Mech_MovementTick
entries.description: Per-tick mech physics step: push transform, integrate motion, clamp Z to Terrain_HeightQuery plus typeRec[+0x16], collision test, restore and reverse speed on hit, place legs. Dispatched via mech vtable +0x18 to 00415b38 to behaviour struct +0x18; its pointer lives in an unmarked 0x24-stride table from 00499928, so Ghidra reports zero xrefs.

entries.name: Mech_IntegrateMotion
entries.description: Sets the animation playback rate from mech+0x2a0, then advances the object by dt = Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(100) via SimObject_ApplyRootMotion.

entries.name: SimObject_ApplyRootMotion
entries.description: Seeds the shape root node to identity, advances the animation by dt, reads node 0 world transform back, and applies it: pos = objRotation * delta.translation + pos, euler += eulerOf(delta.rotation). Then resets the root. The only source of Herc translation and turn-in-place rotation.

entries.name: SimObject_PushTransform
entries.description: Saves the object transform, position and the whole animated node hierarchy into globals at 004a8d54. Paired with SimObject_PopTransform.

entries.name: SimObject_PopTransform
entries.description: Restores what SimObject_PushTransform saved. Used by Mech_MovementTick to undo a blocked move.

entries.name: Mech_CollisionTest
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the just-integrated position is blocked.

entries.name: Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround
entries.description: Per-leg terrain placement over the mech animated node hierarchy.

entries.name: AnimThread_LoadFrameGroundMovement
entries.description: Called on every animation frame advance. If the sequence ground-movement flag is set, loads Transforms[transformIndices[frame * numParts]] -- part index 0, the root node -- into the thread ground translation (+0x22/24/26) and rotation (+0x28/2a/2c) and sets the ground-move flag at +0x20.

entries.name: AnimThread_ReadRootTransform
entries.description: Returns scale(groundTransform, thread[0x1c]/thread[0x1e]) composed onto the thread stored transform, where the fraction is intra-frame accumulator over frame duration. Inverse of AnimThread_WriteRootTransform.

entries.name: AnimThread_WriteRootTransform
entries.description: Stores inverse(scale(groundTransform, frac)) composed with the incoming transform. Paired with AnimThread_ReadRootTransform so that seeding identity and reading back yields the exact per-tick root-motion delta.

entries.name: AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement
entries.description: On frame exit, folds the completed frame full ground transform into the thread stored transform.

entries.name: AnimThread_UncommitGroundMovement
entries.description: Inverse of AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement, for backward playback.

entries.name: AnimThread_Advance
entries.description: Advances one animation thread by dt * thread[0x4e] >> 8, crossing frames forward or backward and driving the ground-movement load and commit hooks.

entries.name: AnimThread_SetPlaybackRate
entries.description: Writes the playback rate to thread+0x4e; restarts the sequence when the sign flips.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_StepAnimation
entries.description: Advance threads, evaluate keyframes into per-node local transforms, rebuild world transforms. FULLY RESOLVED 2026-08-22, in call order: AnimThread_StepAll (004789a0) then ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals (004789f4, which runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals per thread) then ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms (00478b58). The keyframe interpolation is the middle step, so poses are re-blended every time this is called. CADENCE SETTLED: the sole caller is SimObject_ApplyRootMotion (0040250c), which Mech_IntegrateMotion runs once per sim tick -- poses are evaluated per TICK, not per rendered frame. DBSIM has no separate render rate to be per-frame at: FUN_004677bc spin-waits the whole loop to 40 ms (25 Hz), so tick and frame are the same thing in the original. A port with a fixed 25 Hz tick matches vanilla pose cadence exactly, however fast it renders.

entries.name: Time_BeginSimTick
entries.description: Spins until 40 ms have elapsed (25 Hz frame cap), then sets SimTickDelta = clamp((elapsedMs << 8) / 125, 0x40, 0x1c2). SimTickDelta is Q8 with 1.0 = 125 ms, so rate units are per-125 ms.

entries.name: ThrottleLeverMode
entries.description: Joystick throttle-lever mode: 0 = no lever (keyboard/plain stick), +1 = lever present, -1 = lever present with its sense inverted. Set by FUN_00459d20, which writes 1 only when the input config reports a throttle control AND the preferences page assigns it to THROTTLE rather than TURRET, and 0 otherwise; the key command (Sim_PollPlayerInput case 5) and the cockpit slider commit (FUN_00448378) only flip between +1 and -1 and are gated on that same pair. NOT a forward/reverse gear selector, which is what this symbol was called until 2026-08-21 -- DBSIM has no gear. In Mech_ApplyThrottleInput it gates two things: the absolute-lever read (|axis-0x100|*2, deadbanded below 100) and the throttle clamp, which spans the full +/-0x400 at 0 and closes to one side of zero otherwise. That is why holding the keyboard throttle down walks a HERC through zero into reverse.

entries.name: PlayerMech
entries.description: The player-controlled mech. Distinct from LocalPlayerMech (004d256a, the camera subject). Used for team comparisons, scoring, and to skip Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance for the player.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoTwistTick
entries.description: Torso/turret twist (yaw): rate at mech+0x294, angle at mech+0x298, clamped to +/- typeRec[+0x22]. Rates dt-scaled via Math_IntegrateRateOverTick. Only ACCELERATION is rate-limited -- when |Q8(axis, typeRec[+0x1e])| <= |rate| the rate snaps to it, so releasing or reversing the stick stops the turret dead. Args are (mech, axis, snapTarget, snapEnable); with snapEnable set the turret stops on the tick its angle crosses snapTarget, which is how Mech_CenterTorsoTick lands on centre. Ends by seeking the twist thread (mech+0x230) to (unsigned)angle >> 2 via AnimThread_SeekToPosition -- the turret has no rotation of its own. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_TorsoPitchTick
entries.description: Torso/turret pitch: rate at mech+0x296, angle at mech+0x29a, clamped to the asymmetric range [typeRec+0x2c, typeRec+0x2a]. Same shape as Mech_TorsoTwistTick, on the pitch thread (mech+0x234) and typeRec[+0x24..+0x2c]. Its third argument is the range to the current target, passed straight to FUN_0041a74c for gun convergence. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: AnimThread_SeekToPosition
entries.description: Parks a thread at a Q14 fraction of a sequence instead of playing through it: sums the sequence's frame durations, scales the position by Q14 x (total - 1) (FUN_0047dfb4), walks the frames subtracting durations, and installs the resulting frame + intra-frame offset with AnimThread_SetSequence (004791a0). The only caller pair is the two torso ticks, which pass (unsigned)angle >> 2 -- this is how a turret angle becomes a pose. See docs/simulation/torso-aim.md.

entries.name: Mech_CenterTorsoTick
entries.description: The [Backspace] 'Center Turret' command, run every tick while DAT_004d2588 is latched. Drives each torso tick with -clamp(Q10(0xfa, angle), +/-0x100) and snapTarget 0 with the snap enabled, so the turret runs home and stops exactly on centre. Nothing clears the mode on arrival; the input path clears it the moment either turret axis is non-zero.

entries.name: maybe_Mech_ConvergeGunsOnRange
entries.description: Run from Mech_TorsoPitchTick with the range to the current target. Walks the mech's gun list (mech+0x202) and writes a per-gun aim vector at gun+0x24/+0x28, built from the gun's own muzzle position (FUN_0040f540) offset by record field 100; a range of 0 zeroes it instead. Named from that structural role -- the vector's consumer was not traced. Not ported.

entries.name: Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle
entries.description: Returns mech+0x298. Mech vtable slot +0x3c; the Center Body command (scancode 0x2b) uses it to work out the heading the legs must turn to.

entries.name: g_CenterTurretMode
entries.description: Latched by scancode 0x0e ([Backspace]) and by the expiry of the timer at mech+0x31b; cleared by scancode 0x2b (Center Body) and by Sim_PollPlayerInput the moment either turret axis is non-zero. While set, the player's turret block runs Mech_CenterTorsoTick instead of the two torso ticks.

entries.name: g_CenterBodyMode
entries.description: The counterpart of g_CenterTurretMode for scancode 0x2b ('\', Center Body): while set, Sim_PollPlayerInput steers the machine onto the turret's centreline instead of taking the throttle/steer axes, using the target heading cached in g_CenterBodyTargetHeading (004d2af8). Cleared only by its own convergence test or by [Backspace]; steering and the turret axes do not cancel it.

entries.name: Cockpit_TargetAnglesFromCameraBone
entries.description: Transforms a world point into the pilot eye's frame and returns its azimuth/elevation. CameraBoneId (typeRec+0x0c) is a shape PART id: the shape find-by-id vtable slot (+0x20) returns the part, its TSBasePart.Transform (+4) is a transform id, and that indexes the per-node transform array at shapeInst+0x16 (0x20 bytes per entry). Composes the inverse of the mech transform (mech+0xc) then the inverse of that node transform, and subtracts typeRec+0x66. The cockpit eye rides the same node, which is where the retail cockpit bob comes from -- no dedicated bob code exists. Chain is uniform across the fleet: part 5 -> transform 11 -> 4 -> 1 for 16 of 18 HERCs, node 1 being the one the walk cycle animates.

entries.name: maybe_MechBehaviourTable
entries.description: Start of an unmarked 0x24-stride table of per-mech-type behaviour structs; slot +0x18 holds Mech_MovementTick (18 entries located by raw byte search).

entries.name: SliderWidget_CtorBase
entries.description: Shared slider base ctor (obj, trackRect, min, max, initial, knobSize). Sets the widget's +0x1d drag flag to 1 unconditionally -- the ONLY ctor traced that does, and therefore the whole reason the throttle slider is the one draggable control in a retail cockpit. Widget_OnMouseDown (004527a0) tests that flag before latching Widget_DragCapture.

entries.name: SliderWidget_DragToPointV
entries.description: Vertical slider drag handler (vtable +0x18). Saves the previous knob position to +0x2a, clamps the pointer y into [trackTop + knobHeight, trackBottom], and stores it as the knob's BOTTOM edge at +0x28 -- so grabbing the knob jumps its lower edge under the cursor. Horizontal twin is 004524f8.

entries.name: SliderWidget_GetValueV
entries.description: Vertical slider get-value (vtable +0x10): (knobTop(+0x32) - trackTop(+4)) * 0x10000 / scale(+0x20) + min(+0x24). Reads the knob's TOP against the track's top while SetValueV places its BOTTOM, so it returns the NEGATION of what SetValueV was given (for the symmetric +/-0x400 range). Not a bug: ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue negates again, and the two cancel. Horizontal twin is 00452544, which is self-consistent.

entries.name: SliderWidget_SetValueV
entries.description: Vertical slider set-value (vtable +0x14): knobBottom(+0x28) = trackBottom(+0xc) - ((value - min) * scale >> 16), then dispatches the commit slot (+8). Max puts the knob at the track top. Horizontal twin is 0045255c.

entries.name: SliderWidget_RecomputeScaleV
entries.description: Vertical slider scale (vtable +0x1c): +0x20 = ((trackBottom - knobHeight) - trackTop) * 0x10000 / (max - min), i.e. Q16 device pixels per value unit over the knob's travel. Horizontal twin is 004525a8.

entries.name: Widget_DragCapture
entries.description: Set by Widget_OnMouseDown when the pressed widget's +0x1d flag is 1. While set, CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue routes every position change to the captured widget's drag slot (+0x18) WITHOUT hit-testing -- a drag follows the pointer off the widget and off the window -- and the release path reads the value (+0x10) and commits it (+8) instead of calling Widget_OnMouseUp, so a drag fires no click.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_CtorV
entries.description: The throttle's vertical slider child, built when .GAU offset 1064 (SLIDE_DIR) == 1 -- the case all 9 retail .GAU files use. Knob spans the track's full width with its height from throttle bank frame 1 (28x12), limits +/-0x400 at +0x24/+0x26, and an initial position centred on the track (knobBottom = trackBottom - (trackHeight - knobHeight)/2), which is the manual's centred-is-stopped detent. Also constructs the two LED fill bars from .GAU ints [8..11] and [12..15] into private fields +0x7e and +0x82 -- it never registers them as children, and nothing ever paints them (see LedBarGraph_CtorV).

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_CtorFixed
entries.description: The SLIDE_DIR != 1 throttle slider variant: a fixed 12px-wide knob centred horizontally and spanning the track's full height. No retail .GAU selects it (all 9 hold 1 at offset 1064), so this branch is never exercised by retail data and its behaviour is unverified.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_OnValue
entries.description: Throttle slider commit slot (vtable +8). Notifies the parent gauge via FUN_0043904c (which dispatches the owner's slot 0 = ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue, then repaints), then sets ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) from the sign of the committed value -- but gated on a joystick throttle control being configured AND assigned to THROTTLE in preferences, so it is inert on a keyboard/mouse setup.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_SetValues
entries.description: Writes the gauge's live value pair at +0xb1 from a caller struct of two ints: [0] speed as a Q10 fraction of max, [1] throttle Q10 +/-0x400. Pushes the throttle down to the slider child's set-value slot (+0x14) when it changed, and marks the child dirty (+0x1f = 2) when the speed fraction changed. Called once a frame by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_GetValues
entries.description: Returns gauge + 0xb1, the speedFraction/throttle int pair. Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate reads [1] (gauge+0xb5) into mech+0x290 unless the mech+0x93 dirty flag says input moved the throttle this frame, in which case it pushes the other way. That arbitration is the whole of the two-way binding between the slider and the keyboard.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_OnChildValue
entries.description: Gauge slot 0: a child reporting a value. Finds the child in the gauge's array (+0x18, count +0x68); index 0 is the slider, and its value is negated when the gauge's +0xc1 is 0 (the vertical variant) before being stored to +0xb5. That negation cancels SliderWidget_GetValueV's own inversion, leaving positive = forward = knob up.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_CtorV
entries.description: Vertical LED bar graph ctor (obj, rect, range) -- the V twin of LedBarGraph_CtorBase (004390c4), taking start/end from the rect's y0/y1 instead of x0/x1. The throttle gauge builds two: .GAU ints [8..11] with range +0x400 (forward fill, above centre) and [12..15] with -0x400 (reverse fill, below). This is what those ints are; they are NOT the four detent points HThrottle previously recorded. NEITHER THROTTLE BAR IS EVER DRAWN: the slider holds them privately, ThrottleSlider_PaintV reads them only for their rects (via FUN_004390b8) to widen the region it invalidates, and the bar draw routines 00439398/00439460 have no callers in the image. A cut feature, along with the gauge+0xb1 speed fraction that would have filled them.

entries.name: Input_SetThrottleLeverMode
entries.description: Sets ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) to 1 only when the input config struct (FUN_004777f8) reports a throttle control at +2 AND the caller's mode == 1 (the preferences page's THROTTLE rather than TURRET assignment); 0 otherwise. This is the function that proves 0049a06e is a joystick-lever mode and not a forward/reverse gear -- with no lever it is 0, which leaves Mech_ApplyThrottleInput's clamp spanning the full +/-0x400 so the keyboard can reach reverse.

entries.name: AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals
entries.description: THE KEYFRAME INTERPOLATOR -- resolves 2026-08-22 the open 'no interpolator was found in DBSIM' question. For each animated column of the playing sequence, reads the transform-pool index at (sequence, frame) and at (nextSequence, nextFrame); if the two indices match, copies the 12-byte local transform straight; otherwise calls Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms (00492600) with a Q10 interpolant of ((frameAccumulator * 0x400 + frameDuration/2) / frameDuration) -- the SAME elapsed-frame fraction AnimThread_ReadRootScaled already ramps root motion by. Writes into the shape instance's per-node local array (shapeInst+0x12, stride 0xc, indexed by transform id) and sets that node's dirty byte in shapeInst+0xe. Columns whose part id is 0 are skipped entirely, so transform 0 keeps its default and never takes an animated pose. Thread field offsets confirmed here: +4 sequence, +6 frame, +8 nextSequence, +10 nextFrame, +0x1c frameAccumulator, +0x1e frameDuration.

entries.name: Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms
entries.description: Blends two 12-byte ANAnimListTransform records (3 euler shorts then 3 translation shorts) by a Q10 factor (0x400 == fully the second). Rotation components take the SHORTEST ARC: the difference is biased by 0x10000 when it would go negative, subtracted, then folded back by 0x10000 when it exceeds 0x7fff -- the same wrap BinaryAngle.Delta performs -- before the Q10 multiply and arithmetic >>10. Translation components are a plain truncating lerp on the 16-bit difference. All fixed point; no float anywhere.

entries.name: ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms
entries.description: Composes the per-node WORLD transform array (shapeInst+0x16, stride 0x20, indexed by transform id) that everything else reads -- e.g. Mech_TargetRelativeToPilot (0041ef14) and the cockpit eye. Walks the relation list (pairs of shorts at animList+0xc, count at animList+10): parent == -1 goes through ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform (00478b10), otherwise ShapeInst_ComposeChildTransform (00478ab8) against the parent's already-built world transform. Dirty-flag driven off shapeInst+0xe (bit 0 = local changed, bit 1 = world rebuilt, so children follow), and memsets the flag array when done.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform
entries.description: Expands one 12-byte local transform into a 0x20-byte world transform with no parent: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 over the three leading shorts, and the trailing three shorts widened to the ints at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c. Confirms the 0xc-byte local record layout is [eulerX, eulerY, eulerZ, x, y, z] as shorts.

entries.name: ShapeInst_ComposeChildTransform
entries.description: Same expansion as ShapeInst_ExpandRootTransform, then concatenates the result onto the parent's world transform (FUN_0047f914) into the destination slot. The parent-chain composition Herculan's AnimationThread.NodeTransform performs lazily per requested node.

entries.name: ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals
entries.description: Runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals (004799a4) over every thread the shape instance holds (thread pointers from shapeInst+0x1a upward), passing the local-transform array (shapeInst+0x12) and the dirty-flag array (shapeInst+0xe). The loop runs last-to-first; the natural reading is that it lets an earlier thread win a node a later one also writes, but that ordering intent was not independently confirmed.

entries.name: AnimThread_StepAll
entries.description: Advances every thread on the shape instance by the timestep (AnimThread_Advance, 00479614), bracketed by FUN_004788a4/FUN_004788c4 (thread-list iteration helpers, not further decoded). Then, if a first thread exists, writes its ramped root transform (00478fa8 = AnimThread_ReadRoot) into the leading slot of the world-transform array at shapeInst+0x16.

entries.name: TSGroup_RenderPolys
entries.description: DBSIM's counterpart to VSHELL's symbol of the same name, and the same field layout: +0x10 Indexes (defaulted when null), +0x14 Points, +0x18 Surfaces, +0x22 colorCount (memset size for the scratch buffer), +0x1c Polys walked as object pointers, +0x26 Polys.Length. Loop body calls each poly's vtable slot +0x1c. Opens by calling TSGroup_BindNodeTransform (00476014), which is what places the group's geometry at its own animated node -- see docs/formats/dts-node-posing.md. FUN_004758ce is the same function reached mid-prologue.

entries.name: TSGroup_BindNodeTransform
entries.description: One-line forwarder: ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform(group, out, (short)*(group + 4)). Field +4 is TSBasePart.Transform, the same transform id CameraBoneId resolves to through a part -- so every geometry group is drawn through its own node. See docs/formats/dts-node-posing.md.

entries.name: ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform
entries.description: For a non-negative transform id: FUN_0047f914(g_ShapeNodeWorldTransforms + id * 0x20, maybe_g_ShapeObjectToViewTransform, out) then installs the result via maybe_Raster_SetModelTransform (0048c338). Guarded by the per-node cache flags at &DAT_006bb334, so several groups on one node compose once. A negative id skips the composition and leaves the standing transform. This is the whole of how an animated node moves geometry -- see docs/formats/dts-node-posing.md.

entries.name: ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray
entries.description: Binds the shape instance's per-node world transform array (shapeInst+0x16) to the render-side global g_ShapeNodeWorldTransforms, and on a non-null bind clears the 0x32-byte per-node cache-flag block at &DAT_006bb334 and resets the render-context stack index DAT_006bb368. Called before a shape's groups are drawn.

entries.name: g_ShapeNodeWorldTransforms
entries.description: Pointer to the currently bound shape instance's per-node WORLD transform array (shapeInst+0x16, stride 0x20, indexed by transform id -- the array ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms fills). Written only by ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray (00475fd8); read by ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform (00476030) and by FUN_00476a1c.

entries.name: g_ShapeNodeTransformCacheFlags
entries.description: 0x32-byte per-node 'already composed for this shape' flag block, cleared by ShapeInst_BindNodeTransformArray. Byte 0 is set as a bound marker; the per-node flags ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform tests start at 006bb335 and are indexed by transform id.

entries.name: maybe_g_ShapeObjectToViewTransform
entries.description: The transform a node's world transform is composed WITH in ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform, i.e. the object-to-view step. Sits at &DAT_006b7bf4 + 0x20, inside element 0 of the 0x110-stride render-context array allocated by FUN_00476b64 (Cpp_VectorNew(&DAT_006b7bf4, 0x110, 0x34, ...)). The role is inferred from that single read -- no writer was located, so the name is a maybe_.

entries.name: g_CenterBodyTargetHeading
entries.description: Short. Latched by scancode 0x2b to (mech+0x10) - Mech_GetTorsoTwistAngle() -- the world direction the turret is pointing in at the moment Center Body is pressed. While g_CenterBodyMode is set, both the substituted steering command and the substituted turret twist command are errors measured against this one number.

entries.name: Sim_ExecuteCommand
entries.description: Keyboard command dispatch, switched on scancode. Called both from the key queue and directly by Sim_PollPlayerInput (which passes 0x14 for one of the MFD cases). Case 0x0e/0x14 latch g_CenterTurretMode and clear g_CenterBodyMode; case 0x2b does the reverse and caches g_CenterBodyTargetHeading. Both also clear the auto-turret-tracking flag at mech+0x202 -> +0x14.

entries.name: Mech_GetSpeed
entries.description: Mech vtable slot +0x38 (vtable 0049a282). Returns Q10(2000, mech+0x28e) for a walker, or mech+0x2bd when the type record's flyer flag (+0x50) is set. Used for its sign by the Center Body branch, and as a speed term by the AI's lead-the-target maths.

entries.name: ThrottleSlider_PaintV
entries.description: Vertical throttle slider paint. Copies the gauge's +0xb1 speed fraction into +0x7a/+0x4a and does nothing further with it, reads the two LED fill bars' rects only to widen the invalidated region handed to FUN_0043122c, then blits the knob at its current height. It never draws either bar -- see LedBarGraph_CtorV.

entries.name: Gunsight_AddChild
entries.description: Appends a child pointer to the roving-gunsight complex's array at widget+0xd7 (count at +0xff), so construction order is child index. Gunsight_Paint (0043d5c8) walks that array calling each child's slot 0.

entries.name: Gunsight_Paint
entries.description: Paints the front-window HUD: every child of the array at widget+0xd7 in order, then the mission-name label and the speed readout.

entries.name: Gunsight_SetValues
entries.description: Called once a frame by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate with the machine's heading (mech+0x10), turret twist (+0x298) and turret pitch (+0x29a). Caches them at widget+0xb1/+0xb3/+0xb5 and forwards each one's delta to a child's AddDelta slot (+0xc): heading -> child 7 as (new - old), twist -> child 2 (the rotation indicator) as (old - new), pitch -> child 3 as (old - new).

entries.name: HudSlideBar_CtorBase
entries.description: Base of the front-window HUD's sliding-bar widgets. Stores the rect, defaults the limits to +/-0x4800 at +0x24/+0x26, precomputes the range at +0x2c and seeds the current value at +0x3a to the midpoint. HudSlideBar_SetLimits (0043b3c0) is the vtable +0x10 slot that overrides those limits.

entries.name: HudSlideBar_SetLimits
entries.description: Slide-bar vtable slot +0x10: sets min/max at +0x24/+0x26, recomputes the range and the midpoint value, then runs the recompute slot (+8). The gunsight gives the heading tape and child 7 +/-0xe38 (~20 deg) and the rotation indicator +/-0x38e3 (~80 deg).

entries.name: HudSlideBar_AddDelta
entries.description: Slide-bar vtable slot +0xc: value (+0x3a) -= delta, clamped to [+0x24, +0x26]. The only caller is Gunsight_SetValues, which chooses the delta's sign per child so that a bar either tracks its angle or scrolls against it.

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Ctor
entries.description: The manual's Rotation Indicator -- child 2 of the roving-gunsight complex, driven by the turret twist angle. Has no .GAU rect of its own: Gau_RovingGunsightWidget derives it from the heading tape's rect at offset 1104 with literals (+15, -10, 90 wide, 4 tall) and then gives it limits +/-0x38e3.

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Recompute
entries.description: Slide-bar slot +8 for the rotation indicator: caches the rect's width at +0x28 as the bar's travel, and the track sprite's blit position at +0x2e/+0x32 -- the rect's top-left lifted by (2 << VideoMode_YCoordShift).

entries.name: HudRotationIndicator_Paint
entries.description: Blits HUD bank frame 11 (182x10) as the track, then the sliding bar: frame 13 (green) while |value| <= 299, frame 12 (yellow) otherwise, at rect.x0 + (value - min) * width / range, minus (15 << VideoMode_XCoordShift) to centre the 62px bar on that point. This is the manual's 'turns yellow and moves left or right if your Turret moves from center'.

entries.name: HudSlideBar_CtorHidden
entries.description: Child 3 of the roving-gunsight complex, driven by the turret pitch angle. Its vtable (0049c20c) has no-op stubs in both the paint (0043b574) and recompute (0043b56c) slots, so the pitch axis has a slide bar that is never drawn -- there is no on-screen pitch indicator.

entries.name: maybe_Raster_SetModelTransform
entries.description: Installs a 0x20-byte transform as the rasterizer's current model transform: stores the pointer in DAT_006c607c (defaulting to &DAT_006c6080 when null), composes it with DAT_006c6078 into the derived chain at &DAT_006c6038/&DAT_006c6058, and rebuilds the dependent state. Called by ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform and by every other site that changes what space geometry is submitted in. The derived globals were not individually decoded, hence medium.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeReactorRate
entries.description: Computes the mech reactor output rate into mech+0x256. Base is a literal 0x14 (20) shared by the whole fleet -- the type record is never read. Replaced outright by Q10(200,20)=3 when mech+0xab (reactor critical) or Q10(600,20)=11 when mech+0xaa (reactor degraded). An Energy Pod in slot mech+0x313 then adds Q10(1024 - 204*(podDamage/51), 20), up to a second full 20 (it doubles output), gated off entirely at 225/256 damage. ONE reference in the whole binary, the tail of Mech_ConfigureLoadout, so the rate is sampled at spawn and never recomputed.

entries.name: Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity
entries.description: Sibling of Mech_ComputeReactorRate for shield capacity; writes mech+0x228 via Shield_SetMax. Base is typeRecord+0xc0 = record offset 190 = HercSimDat.ShieldMaxTotal, a fleet-wide 3500. Chassis damage above 0x80 on dependent-subpiece 4 scales it down in five steps to 50%; a Shield Pod in slot mech+0x30f adds up to a second full base (doubling it) on the same five-step pod-damage curve the Energy Pod uses. Called once, from Mech_ConfigureLoadout, followed by Shield_RefillToBalance.

entries.name: MechLoadout_FileEquipmentPods
entries.description: Walks the finished weapon-mount list and files five specific weapon ids into the five-pointer pod array at mech+0x307, keyed on the mount template's +0x56 (the SHELL0 gam/WEAPONS.DAT catalog id, written as the record index by Weapons_LoadResourceTables). Slot order is not id order: 0x12 ECM->[0], 0x1d TARG->[1], 0x1e SHLD->[2], 0x20 ENRG->[3], 0x1f TURB->[4]. Assigns rather than accumulates, so a duplicate pod contributes nothing.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ArbitrateEnergy
entries.description: Vtable slot 0 of the weapon-mount-manager at mech+0x202 for both manager classes; the weapon half of the Master Energy Pool tick. Serves the player's selected mount first (manager+0x1d; AI passes -1), then the remaining mounts highest-priority-first by vtable+0x48. Each mount takes its share via vtable+0x34 and passes the remainder on. Once any mount reports itself mid-charge (+0x43), every later mount targets zero instead and bleeds its capacitor back to the pool, so only one energy weapon charges at a time. Returns the unclaimed budget. A player-only infinite-energy debug path refunds all consumption when DAT_004a9ed6==0 and DAT_004a9edc==1.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ChargeCapacitor
entries.description: One energy mount's draw on the pool. Target is the mount's capacity (+0x7b), or zero when told another mount is already charging, minus its stored charge (+0x7d); takes min(chargeRate +0x7f, budget, deficit) and returns the remainder. A non-positive deficit clears the charging flag (+0x43) and bleeds charge back at up to 5/tick. PLAS (catalog id 25) is half-efficiency: its deficit counts double and only half the drawn energy is stored. Ammunition mounts override this with a no-op that consumes nothing.

entries.name: Shield_SetMax
entries.description: Trivial setter: writes the shield array's total capacity at shieldStruct+6 (mech+0x228). Only caller is Mech_ComputeShieldCapacity. The base capacity at shieldStruct+8 is left alone, which is why the cockpit rings measure against the pre-pod figure.

entries.name: Shield_RefillToBalance
entries.description: Fills the shield array to its max and splits it at the current balance: front = Q10(balance, max), rear = max - front. Called from Mech_ConfigureLoadout right after Shield_SetMax, so a mech spawns with full shields at whatever capacity its pods bought it.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetEnergyPriority
entries.description: Vtable+0x48 on energy mounts: returns the mount's capacity (+0x7b), or 10000 when its charging flag (+0x43) is set so a mount already mid-charge jumps the arbitration queue and finishes charging. The ammunition mount class returns 0 from this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetDisplayName
entries.description: The name a weapon gauge prints for a mount. If the mount's resolved PROJ.DAT record (+0x20) is null or its category is non-zero, copies the template's name pointer (+0x52, written by Weapons_LoadResourceTables from the 33-entry array at 00498eb0). If the record is a Missile (category 0), copies MissileAmmoNameTable[record.subtypeId] instead -- so a launcher is named by its loaded ammunition (ARH, SARH, ...), not by its weapon id. Returns a pointer to the shared scratch buffer at 004a9954.

entries.name: WeaponMountNameTable
entries.description: 33 char* in weapon-id order -- the simulator's own weapon names, walked by Weapons_LoadResourceTables into each WeaponMountTemplate's +0x52. NOT the SHELL0/GAM/WEAPONS.DAT catalog's names: id 7 is 'EMP' here and 'EMPC' there, id 30 'SHIELD' vs 'SHLD'. Ids 13-16 hold bare round counts ('6','8','10','24') because a launcher never prints this name.

entries.name: MissileAmmoNameTable
entries.description: 4 char* indexed by a PROJ.DAT Missile record's subtype id: SARH, ARH, ARM, EO. Read only by WeaponMount_GetDisplayName, with no bounds check -- MISSL (id 21, subtype 4) reads one past the end.

entries.name: GunLayout_LoadForMechType
entries.description: Loads one gl\<HERC>.GL hardpoint list into the object pool slot for a mech type: short count, then count 26-byte records. Asserts in GUNLIST.CPP. The record's byte at +0x17 indexes the mission's loadout arrays and its byte at +7 is the cockpit weapon row the resulting mount owns.

entries.name: GunLayout_GetBySlot
entries.description: index * 6 + _DAT_004a9968 -- flat index into the loaded gun-layout table. Each 6-byte entry is {short count, record*}. Callers reach it through FUN_00420634, which adds the mech type's own allocation index to the base slot cached in _DAT_004a9df4.

entries.name: Mech_GetGunLayout
entries.description: GunLayout_GetBySlot(mechTypeRecord[0] + _DAT_004a9df4) -- this machine's hardpoint list. Its return value is what Mech_ConfigureLoadout hands MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts as the record array and count.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorAmmunition
entries.description: Ammunition mount constructor (vtable 00498d54): reads the magazine size from the template's +0x3a into +0x7b and the same value shifted left 8 into +0x7d, so the mount powers up with a full magazine and its gauge prints +0x7d >> 8. Used for weapon ids 1-5, 13-16, 21 and 26.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorEnergy
entries.description: Energy mount constructor (vtable 00498dcc): writes Q10Multiply(820, 1200) = 960 into both the charge target (+0x7b) and the capacitor level (+0x7d), and 20 into the charge rate (+0x7f). All three are literals shared by every energy weapon. Used for weapon ids 6-12, 17, 19, 20 and 22-25, 28.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState
entries.description: Energy mount vtable+0x50, called once per mount per frame from WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate. Pushes (charge << 10) / 1200 as the LED bar's value and the charge target scaled the same way as its tick mark, plus the destroyed and mid-charge flags and the three caller-supplied bytes (selected, in current fire group, ready). The fixed 1200 denominator -- not the mount's own capacity -- is why a fully charged weapon fills four-fifths of its bar.

entries.name: WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x50, the sibling of WeaponMount_PushEnergyGaugeState. Decays +0x7d toward capacity*256 at 250/tick if it is above it, then pushes +0x7d >> 8 as the round count the gauge prints, plus the destroyed flag and the three caller-supplied state bytes.

entries.name: WeaponMount_EnergyCanFire
entries.description: Energy mount vtable+0x2c: not destroyed (+0x49), refire timer (+0x31) expired, and charge (+0x7d) at or above a threshold taken from the template's +0x36/+0x38 pair -- max(+0x36, +0x7b) when +0x36 < +0x38, otherwise +0x38 outright. Both shapes occur in retail data (EMP 350/10000, ELF 400/70).

entries.name: WeaponMount_AmmoCanFire
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x2c: not destroyed (+0x49), refire timer (+0x31) expired, and at least one round left (+0x7b != 0).

entries.name: WeaponMount_GetAmmoType
entries.description: Ammunition mount vtable+0x60: returns the resolved PROJ.DAT record's subtype id when that record is a Missile (category 0), otherwise 5. Callers treat 5 and 3 as always-available and gate the other values on the manager's per-ammunition-type counters at manager+0x0a. The energy class returns a constant 5 from this slot (FUN_0040e62c).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_CtorLocal
entries.description: The locally-piloted machine's mount manager (vtable 00499238): runs MechLoadout_ConstructWeaponMounts, then allocates three fire-group arrays (manager+0x1f/+0x25/+0x2b) and picks the initial selection. Writes 'group == wanted' into all three arrays with wanted fixed at 0 for a weapon and -1 for a pod, so every non-pod mount starts in group I and groups II and III start empty; manager+0x1d becomes the first non-pod mount in mount-array order.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate
entries.description: The mount manager's per-frame pass: reads the weapon-panel input block, applies the chain/link commands, then walks every mount and calls its vtable+0x50 gauge push with three state bytes -- selected (index == manager+0x1d), in the current fire group (groups[manager+0x1c][index]), and ready (WeaponMounts_MountIsReady).

entries.name: WeaponMounts_MountIsReady
entries.description: The readiness flag a weapon row's state box is lit by: the mount's own vtable+0x2c test, gated on target range when manager+0x31 is set, then gated again on ammunition availability -- vtable+0x60's code is taken as always-available for 5 and 3, and otherwise checked against manager[0x0a + code*2]. No writer for that counter array was found along the paths traced.

entries.name: PodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for equipment pods (vtable 0049c8d0), built via FUN_004321d4. Has no state box and no value field: its name label spans x0+11..x0+53 of the .GAU hardpoint rect, and its 11-char name buffer is seeded with a literal space, then the mount name, then STRINGS0.STR group 3 (' POD') appended into whatever room is left -- 'SHIELD' becomes ' SHIELD POD'.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for ammunition mounts (vtable 0049c8fc), built via FUN_00432124. Adds a left-aligned numeric label over the value field at x0+36..x0+53, y0..y0+5 of the .GAU hardpoint rect; FUN_004411b4 fills it with itoa(rounds) in ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when the mount is selected and [11] GRAY otherwise.

entries.name: EnergyWeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The weapon-row gauge class for energy mounts (vtable 0049c91c), built via FUN_00432074. Builds the LED charge bar over the same value field the ammunition class puts its number in (x0+36..x0+53, y0..y0+5), handing it to FUN_00442950.

entries.name: WeaponChargeBar_Ctor
entries.description: The energy weapon row's LED bar widget. Drops the value field's top edge by one GAU unit, builds an LEDBarGraph over range 0x400, and then, when the byte it is handed is zero (as it is in every retail .GAU, where it lands in confirmed-zero padding), overwrites its three colour fields with raw palette indices 0x20 (even columns), 0x22 (odd) and 0x2e (remainder) -- not COLORS.DAT ids, which is why a capacitor bar is blue where the Master Energy Pool's meter is grey.

entries.name: Sim_DispatchCommand
entries.description: The simulator's command dispatcher: every queued command code passes through here. Offers the code to the cockpit widget tree (CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand), then to FUN_0045fd60, then its own switch, and finally to the player mech's vtable +0x2c. Codes are PC set-1 scancodes with 0x200 added for Alt -- 0x26 is L, 0x29 is backquote, 0x11/0x211 are W and Alt+W, 0x02-0x0b and 0x202-0x20b the two number-key banks.

entries.name: Mech_HandleCommand
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x2c. Offers the command code to the machine's weapon-mount manager (WeaponMounts_HandleCommand) first and returns if that consumed it; otherwise handles the turret, throttle and shield commands itself.

entries.name: CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand
entries.description: The cockpit widget tree's command handler. Codes 0x02-0x0b (the number row) index the ten weapon gauges at CockpitViewInstance+0x70 and press each one's select gadget, which is how a number key and a mouse click on a weapon row reach the same handler; F1-F8, the view commands and the shield keys are handled here too, and anything left over is offered to each top-level widget's own command slot.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_HandleCommand
entries.description: The weapon-mount manager's command handler, called from Mech_HandleCommand. 0x202-0x20b (Alt+1..0) toggle a row's fire-chain membership via WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember; 0x11 and 0x211 (W, Alt+W) step the armed weapon via WeaponMounts_StepSelection and clear the single-fire flag at manager+0x18; 0x30 advances the fire chain; 0x2c calls FUN_00410d04; 0xc/0xd/0x4a/0x4e reach the armed mount's vtable +0x38.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember
entries.description: Add or remove one cockpit weapon row from the CURRENT fire chain -- Alt and the row's number key, or a right click on the row. Finds the mount by its .GL fire-chain byte (slot+7), requires the mount template's int32 at 0x30 to be positive (zero for every pod, which is what keeps pods off a chain), then XORs that mount's bit in the current chain array via WeaponMounts_XorChainBit. It does not arm anything. Follows the toggle by waking an energy mount's capacitor when its arbitration priority reads zero.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_XorChainBit
entries.description: Flips one mount's membership bit in the currently selected fire chain (manager+0x1f + manager+0x1c*6, indexed by mount index). Membership is toggled, never set, which is why Alt+number and a right click both add and remove.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge
entries.description: Arm the mount that owns a given weapon gauge -- what a left click on a weapon row and a number key both end at. Finds the mount whose vtable +0x58 gauge-match slot accepts the gauge (the pod base class returns 0 unconditionally, so a pod never matches), requires the mount's selectable byte +0x4c, calls WeaponMounts_SetSelection and sets the single-fire flag at manager+0x18.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetSelection
entries.description: The only writer of the armed-mount index at manager+0x1d. Normalises a linked pair onto its first half: if the mount being armed is linked (+0x4b) and its .GL partner offset (slot+0x16) is negative, the partner is armed instead. That is what keeps a linked pair's two rows agreeing about which of them is armed.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_StepSelection
entries.description: Step the armed mount one place through the current fire chain, wrapping. Skips anything not selectable (+0x4c), not in the current chain, or the second half of a linked pair (partner offset must be positive). Does not clear the single-fire flag itself -- the command handler does, which is why the chain switch and the per-frame advance step the selection without giving the chain control back.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_ToggleLink
entries.description: Toggle link fire on the armed mount and its .GL partner. Two conditions, both from the chassis: the armed mount's slot+0x16 partner offset is non-zero, and the partner hardpoint carries the SAME weapon id (template+0x56). Both halves' +0x4b flip together. One LINK press runs this three times -- the button's click handler, the manager's next per-frame pass reading the button's latch byte, and that pass writing the byte back -- which nets to one flip.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_SetChain
entries.description: Switch which of the three fire chains is current (manager+0x1c). If the armed mount is not in the new chain, steps the selection to one that is, then pushes the new number to the console chain button's caption.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_AdvanceToReady
entries.description: The firing chain's own advance, run every frame from WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate: if the armed mount cannot fire, step through the chain until one that can is found, and put the original back if none is. Gated off entirely while the single-fire flag (manager+0x18) is set, which is the manual's 'select a weapon to single-fire ... once you fire, the current firing chain will resume'.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick
entries.description: The console button panel's child-click slot, switching on the child index: 0 advances the chain number at panel+0xb1 (wrapping at 3) and repaints the caption, 1 calls ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch, 2 toggles auto-track. Reached identically by a mouse click and by a key, since ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand presses the same children.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand
entries.description: The console button panel's command slot: scancode 0x26 (L) presses child 1, the LINK button; 0x29 (backquote) presses child 0, the chain button. The pair of literals is what identifies the whole command-code space as PC set-1 scancodes.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch
entries.description: Stores the LINK button's latch byte at panel+0xb4 and calls WeaponMounts_ToggleLink. Called from the button's own click handler and again from ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock when the manager writes the byte back cleared -- two of the three toggles one press produces.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Copies the console panel's three live fields -- chain number (+0xb1, short), auto-track latch (+0xb3) and LINK latch (+0xb4) -- into the scratch block at 004d1ae0 for WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate to read.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock
entries.description: The write-back half of ConsoleButtons_GetStateBlock: applies each of the three fields that differs from the panel's own copy. The manager clears the LINK byte before writing back, so this sees a change and calls ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch again -- the third of the three toggles one LINK press produces.

entries.name: Widget_GetButtonValue
entries.description: The default GetValue vtable slot (+0x10) for a widget class that does not override it: returns the global mouse-button word 0049db6c, which CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue sets to buttons|1 on a left release and buttons|2 on a right one. A click's 'value' is therefore which button clicked it, and the weapon rows branch on exactly that -- left arms, right toggles chain membership.

entries.name: Widget_PressChild
entries.description: Dispatches one child widget's press slot (+0x17 vtable, +8) as if it had been clicked, then repaints it. This is how a bound key reaches a button: the command handlers call it with the child index rather than duplicating the button's own action.

entries.name: WeaponMount_MatchGaugeNever
entries.description: The pod base class's vtable +0x58 gauge-match slot: returns 0 unconditionally, so WeaponMounts_SelectByGauge can never find a pod. The energy and ammunition classes (FUN_0040df08, FUN_0040df1c) compare the argument against the mount's own gauge pointer at +0x77 instead. Together with the pod constructor clearing the selectable byte +0x4c, this is why a pod's cockpit row cannot be armed.

entries.name: WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x3c: puts the charge target (+0x7b) back to its idle 0x334 unless the mount is destroyed. Called after a chain toggle when the mount reports a zero arbitration priority, so a capacitor that had been zeroed starts asking for charge again. The ammunition and pod classes have a no-op in this slot.

entries.name: WeaponMount_DemandFullCharge
entries.description: Energy mount vtable +0x40: sets the mid-charge flag (+0x43) and raises the charge target (+0x7b) to 0x4b0, the same 1200 the cockpit bar is scaled against -- so only a mount with a shot demanded of it ever fills its bar. Its counterpart WeaponMount_WakeCapacitor drops the target back to the idle 820.
